The workspace's revisions table, (location, id, parent), caches those files and is only added to. revisions() returns every revision, unordered. revision(id) on a miss reads the file and each uncached parent, and raises KeyError where the first file is absent. A concurrent duplicate insert's TransactionException is caught.
  • Parquet goes through DuckDB. The manifest, revision files, listings and existence checks go through Files, with read_text, write_text(..., expect=Version | Absent | None), list and exists.
  • s3:// is remote and a URI without :// is local. Any other scheme raises. Local Files uses pathlib, open(..., "x") for Absent, and a SHA-256 Version checked under a sibling .lock. Remote Files uses boto3 behind datarecord[remote] = ["boto3>=1.35.69"], with IfNoneMatch="*" and IfMatch=<etag>, either failing with 412 PreconditionFailed. A remote Version is the ETag.
  • The manifest is widened by compare-and-swap, and a writer whose swap fails re-reads and checks again.
  • Remote access is configured by the AWS environment alone. DuckDB gets CREATE SECRET (TYPE s3, PROVIDER credential_chain, ...), plus ENDPOINT, URL_STYLE 'path' and CHAIN 'env;config' when AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is set, so no instance-metadata probe hangs. httpfs and boto3 load on the first :// URI, so a local workspace never runs the probe.
  • ws.con is a cursor per thread, from a threading.local subclass. Only a relation has a cursor of its own. Every other object looks up workspace.con per call. A relation, a frame and a WorkingRecord belong to the thread that built them.
  • A frozen node's folded axes and groups become shared tables, dims_{dim}_{id} and group_{name}_{id}, read through cast_declared. {id} is the revision, the base of a WorkingRecord, or uuid5 of a standalone directory's URI. Record.dims builds each frame per access. When two misses race to create one table, the one that fails reads the table the other created.
  • as_relation refuses a relation from another connection or cursor with a ValueError that states the fix.
  • Revision serialises as {"id", "parent", "store"} and validates back through Workspace.process().store(uri).revision(id), the one default left. Store.__reduce__ does the same. Only deserialisation calls it implicitly, and its database does not travel. Code whose records must join deserialised ones calls Workspace.process() by name.
  • A database file is a workspace, never the record. A location is not reused, nor a standalone directory's URI, because datarecord keys caches by id and assumes that an id's content never changes.
  • Record moves to layered/record.py, beside its backing Resolver, and nothing imports back. datarecord/record.py still contains RecordLike, LayerData and their value types, and layered/revision.py still contains Revision and ancestry.
  • Tool.to_datarecord(model, con) and Tool.results(model, con) require con, not a workspace or store, and on_connection goes. build(record) reads record.con.
  • Deleted: DEFAULT_BASE_URI, DATARECORD_BASE_URI, _BASE_URIS, base_uri_of, default_connection, connect, the layer_dir macro, every base_uri=None, read_json, Revision.create, Revision.get, Record.at, Record.over, public write_record, commit, NewChild, Directory, Target and Resolver._cached_dims. write_record, layer_dir, connect, NewChild and Directory leave __all__, and Workspace and Store join it. A function that plans relations, such as fold_axis, keeps its con.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
A required location replaces base_uri=None, which silently meant the process default.

child sits on the parent, because a parent is always its own store's. One call per destination fits destinations that need and return different things.

commit did three jobs, and the caller now does each: picks w.edits or w, names the parent, and calls rollback(). datarecord does not refuse rev.child(w), which writes the whole record as a correct but larger layer.

A revision file per UUID is write-once like a layer, so two processes never write one object. One listing per thousand revisions replaces a read per revision. The revisions cache cannot go stale, because a parent never changes.

boto3 is what Manta already runs, at the cost of its size and of S3 alone. Its conditional writes apply to the revision files and the manifest, but not to the layer, whose parquet DuckDB writes. A fresh UUID and an unreachable failed write cover that.

The guarantees hold only as far as a server honours the headers:

SeaweedFS If-None-Match and If-Match on PutObject before 3.97 ignored 3.97 to 4.17 checked before upload, so two racing writers can both pass (#7154) 4.18 and later checked under the write lock, so exactly one of two racing writers succeeds (#8802)

On Manta's 4.05 the revision files are safe in practice, but the manifest's compare-and-swap can lose a widening, so Manta's pin moves to 4.18 or later. AWS S3 has honoured If-None-Match since August 2024 and If-Match since November 2024.

The tree cannot live only in a DuckDB file, which takes one writer and cannot be remote. A DuckDB file is still useful: staged edits survive a crash, the revisions cache persists, and DuckDB can spill.

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Workspace and Store, the local Files, the tree, cursors, shared fold tables and the deleted globals, in one commit. These parts depend on each other, so a commit with only some of them would leave datarecord broken.
  2. Writing: root, child, ws.write, and edits.
  3. Remote Files and conditional manifest writes.
  4. Tools take con.

On DuckDB 1.5.5, eight threads on their own cursors all succeed. So do sixteen threads taking a first cursor at once, fifty times over.

The remote tests run against SeaweedFS 4.18 or later in a container, because a mock would ignore the headers. New tests check a deserialised revision's ancestry, concurrent reads and cache misses across threads, create-only revision files, two widenings of one manifest, an unlisted revision after a failed remote write, a refused non-empty ws.write, a fold table read under a widened schema, and child(w.edits) on the wrong revision.

The build departed in the remote Files. boto3 uses path-style addressing whenever AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is set. A failure setting up httpfs raises. A 403 on a read or exists counts as a miss, and a 409 counts as a refused write beside 412.

An older location has no revisions/ and reads as an empty tree, fixed by exporting the revisions table as one JSON file per row.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text:
• One object for location and connection: two locations could not join.
  • store.write(source, parent=...) repeats the store, rev.write reads as changing rev, and a target union needs overloads.
  • Revision files inside a layer: a layer directory stays what the layer wrote, and the tree lists in one listing.
  • One revisions.parquet or a shared DuckDB file: not write-once on S3.
  • gen_random_uuid(): the layer directory needs the id before any row exists.
  • fsspec or s3fs has no create-only write, and obstore is a second S3 client.
  • A remote= override: it would not apply to Workspace.process() in a deserialising task.
  • A secret from KEY_ID and SECRET: loses tokens and roles.
  • A dict keyed by threading.get_ident(), whose ids are reused, or a ContextVar, which a task runner copies into workers.
  • A thread check: it misses calls a frame makes on its own cursor.
  • Re-issuing a relation on another cursor: impossible over a Python object.
  • Copying a foreign relation: an unasked-for full materialisation.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• Sweeping orphaned layers of a failed remote write.
  • ws.new(schema), a WorkingRecord with no base.
  • A handle to resume staged edits from a database file.
  • A created field on a revision, and reading over https://.

docs.title: DEP 10: a group is one struct column
DEP 10: a group is one struct column
docs.text:
DEP 10 Title a group is one struct column Author Jonas Hörsch Status Superseded (2026-10-26, implemented 2026-10-12, amended 2026-10-13) Created 2026-10-12 Version Unreleased Superseded-By DEP 20 (its group tombstones, by which the fold drops owner-map rows), DEP 23 (its groups, which become multi-dims)

The design landed in the data model, the record format, the fold, WorkingRecord and tools. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: An attribute over a group has the group as one column, named for the group, of a STRUCT over the group's key: connection STRUCT(entity, bus). The group's coordinates no longer spread out as columns of their own. Every dim a group draws on broadcasts again, and the owner map has one key column per group.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A group in dims expands to its coordinates, so the fold key is the flat union of every group's coordinate names. A column in the fold key is broadcast or membership, never both, and a group coordinate never broadcasts. Schema.broadcast_dims therefore drops every coordinate any group is keyed by, schema-wide.

Attributes that have nothing to do with the group need extra handling. Once connection is over (entity, bus), a NULL bus in a per-bus marginal_price over {bus, timestep} means "no bus". A connection's bus has no axis to expand against, but the dim bus does. The owner map's key, entity | bus | from | to | ..., needs the schema to list which columns identify a connection.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
• A long row has a group as one struct column named for the group, with one field per key coordinate in over order. coordinates_of("efficiency") is ("connection", "timestep").
  • groups/<group>.parquet is keyed by its struct column, as an axis file is keyed by its dim.
  • broadcast_dims loses its exclusion, so bus broadcasts like scenario.
  • The membership keys are entity and one column per group that some long input row carries, which is Schema.group_columns. Adding an attribute stays compatible. In a map folded before a group was added, the fold reads the missing column as NULL. The flag structs gain a field per dim that now broadcasts, such as bus.
  • A group column does not broadcast. It is compared NULL-safely as one value. The fold drops each row whose group column matches one of the group's tombstones.
  • The entity tombstone matches every entity in a row, at the top level and inside each struct. Removing an entity drops its connections' values and leaves the tuples.
  • An attribute over a group and one of its key dims, such as dims={"connection", "bus"}, is refused, because the row would have the bus twice, free to disagree.
  • A group does not share a dim's name, except the entity-type group, which has no file or column.
  • set keeps coordinate keywords: bus="north" packs {entity, bus}.
  • Record.attributes["efficiency"] returns the struct column, and a reader takes struct.field("bus") or unnests. The PyPSA tool packs on to_datarecord and unpacks on build.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
DuckDB 1.5.5 plans k IS NOT DISTINCT FROM k over a STRUCT key as a HASH_JOIN, and a NULL field equals a NULL field. It pushes a struct-field filter into the parquet scan. Over 2M rows in 20 row groups, conn.entity = … and entity = … both read one row group, in 2.0 ms and 1.8 ms.

The design needs a format change to every inputs/ and outputs/ file over a group, and rebuilt owner maps. A numpy-backed pandas frame has no struct dtype, so a pandas reader unnests on the DuckDB side.

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
It landed in four steps: the schema, the fold and read path, staging, then the PyPSA tool. The build added to the argument:

  • Patching a per-bus value one bus at a time needs bus in partial.
  • A value staged without bus= is keyed {entity, NULL} and matches no connection. The reading "every connection of this entity" was never built.
  • A layer's own tombstones apply only to its parents, so remove_group also drops the rows it staged on the tuple.
  • A first cut had remove tombstone every tuple with the entity, which left a re-added entity without its parent's connections.
  • A long frame handed to set has the struct only. Accepting flat coordinates too would have needed a second path with no caller.
  • An empty frame still types the group column as the struct.
  • Shadowing a dim's name went, because a group column and a dim column would share one name.
  • Keying the group file by the struct removed every conversion where a row met it. Packing stays only where a caller hands flat values in, and in the PyPSA tool.
  • The PyPSA tool declares no bus attribute over connection. A port's bus is the connection tuple.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text: • What a value staged without bus= means.

docs.title: Amendment: a group is a dim
docs.text:
Implemented 2026-10-13, drafted the same day.

A group is a dim whose axis is the resolved group, groups/<group>.parquet. It broadcasts, enters the owner map only where partial lists it, and otherwise a layer restates it whole, as it does snapshot.

docs.title: The amended design
docs.text:
• A struct value is a whole tuple or NULL. A NULL struct means every tuple of the group and expands against the resolved group. set, add_group and the writer refuse a partly NULL struct.
  • The membership key is entity alone. A group is keyed in partial_dims exactly where partial lists it.
  • Outside partial, a connection attribute's key is (attribute), so the owner map assigns every connection's value to a layer that touches it. Staging adds the rest of the extent, and a layer written directly has to contain it.
  • In partial, a layer patches one tuple, and the fold drops each parent row that has a tuple a group tombstone names.
  • The flag structs gain a field per group.
  • The PyPSA tool declares connection in partial, so Link.efficiency over snapshot is patched without restating every link.

This replaces "a group column does not broadcast": the fold already has the group's table in Coords.groups. Pulling the struct's entity fields into the key would narrow ownership to one entity's connections. The owner map would then have to key on struct fields, and partial already gives that grain.

The amendment has three costs. flags(ctype) cannot scope a group attribute outside partial, because its map rows contain no entity, so the open question on record-level flags widens. With connection in partial, PyPSA's attributes are unaffected. The owner map's format changes. And a schema that relied on per-connection ownership now has to declare partial={"connection"}.

docs.title: What the amendment found
docs.text:
• expand_dims broadcasts a NULL only on rows whose attribute's coordinates include it, for a dim as for a group. Otherwise every attribute multiplied by the group's size.
  • Removing an entity needs a filter at read, because a connection row outside partial contains no entity. The read drops a row whose unkeyed group field contains an entity the resolved axis no longer has. Since DEP 11, it checks against the group's dead tuples.
  • group_columns stayed, meaning every group but the entity-type group. The derivation of keyed groups went.
  • set's keywords stage no NULL struct, and a missing key coordinate is still refused. A NULL struct comes in through a long frame.
  • The struct change had left src/ about 340 lines larger than the flat layout. The amendment was estimated to remove 40 to 80 lines. Measured, src/ grew by 19 lines net, 119 added and 100 removed, because of the read filter, the scoped expansion and the data check. In return, datarecord has one rule where it had two.

docs.title: What the amendment leaves open
docs.text: • A NULL struct spans entity types: a constant meant for links also applies to buses' connections.

docs.title: DEP 11: deletion cascades through tombstones, not through filters
DEP 11: deletion cascades through tombstones, not through filters
docs.text:
DEP 11 Title deletion cascades through tombstones, not through filters Author Jonas Hörsch Status Implemented (2026-10-13) Requires DEP 10 Created 2026-10-13 Version Unreleased Superseded-By DEP 20 (its removal by tombstone, and dead labels as winning tombstones)

The design landed in layers and the fold. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: A label is removed by a tombstone and only by a tombstone. Removing one tombstones every group tuple that contains it, and a layer that leaves such a tuple alive is refused. A read infers nothing from a dead label that a row refers to. This replaces, for group tuples, the rule of DEP 10 that the tuples stand, dangling.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Removing an entity drops its values in four places, each covering part of the problem:

Where What it drops Keyed on fold_inputs parent owner-map rows hit by this layer's tombstones on entity, groups, partial dims owner-key columns, and entity fields through entity_coordinates _living (read) value rows that set a removed entity on a coordinate outside the owner key the resolved entity axis, through entity_coordinates WorkingRecord._collapsed_inputs staged rows hit by this layer's own entity and tuple tombstones _tombstoned and entity_coordinates resolve_groups only the group's own tombstones none

After remove("Generator", ["g1"]), the value x(g1, bus0) is gone, but the tuple (g1, bus0) still stands in record.groups["connection"]. Every path also goes through entity_coordinates and Schema.entity_fields, which hard-code one dim, so removing a bus label removes nothing inside a struct.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
1. Removing a label writes the cascade. WorkingRecord.remove(ctype, names) tombstones the entities and every group tuple with a field equal to one, read from the resolved groups. The fold applies a group's own tombstones to it, so resolve_groups needs no filter.
  2. write_layer refuses a dangling tuple. A layer that leaves alive a tuple containing a label dead after the layer, or adds a tuple containing one, is refused. A layer written by hand carries its own cascade.
  3. The fold drops keyed values. fold_inputs drops each parent row with a tombstoned label on a coordinate in the owner key. That key is entity and the dims and groups in partial. A re-added label starts fresh. On entity, fold_inputs checks the top-level entity only, and the tuple tombstones of rule 1 cover a group's entity fields.
  4. The read drops unkeyed values against dead labels. For each coordinate outside the owner key, the read drops each value row with a label for which the fold keeps a tombstone. For a group, those are its dead tuples. The read skips this step when there are no such labels.

partial stays the granularity of an override. It is not transitive: a group that draws on a dim in partial need not be in it.

A materialised node has its dead labels in dead/<coord>.parquet, beside dims/ and groups/. It does so for each dim and group outside partial, and for each dim a group draws on. Rule 4 reads the base's dead labels plus those of the layers above. The resolved axes and groups stay tombstone-free, and fold_axis returns the dead labels as a by-product.

_living's filter, the entity-field anti-joins in fold_inputs and _collapsed_inputs, and every literal entity in the cascade go. An anti-join is a query that keeps the rows with no match in another table. entity_coordinates and Schema.entity_fields stay for Fold.flags(ctype) and for set's _keyword_entities.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
Dead labels must survive materialisation. Suppose layer 1 sets x(g1, bus0) with connection outside partial, layer 2 removes g1, and layer 3 is materialised. A read at layer 4 takes x's owner, layer 1, from the cached map. The dead labels of the layers above the base do not include (g1, bus0), so the value would come back. The fold cannot cut it earlier, because along an unkeyed coordinate the owner map has one row per attribute, not per label.

Re-adding a label revives its unkeyed values. Suppose layer 3 re-adds g1 and (g1, bus0). The owner map still lists layer 1 for x, so x(g1, bus0) returns, as does every unkeyed attribute over the tuple. That is what a coordinate outside partial means, To have a re-added label start fresh, you declare the group in partial.

The design has three costs:

  • write_layer depends on the ancestry. Rule 2 is a fold plus a semi-join (a query that keeps the rows that do have a match) per group field.
  • Removing a bus removes its connections, and PyPSA's build reports the component's bus as missing.
  • The resolved cache grows by a dead-labels file per dim and group outside partial.

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• Rule 1 is WorkingRecord.remove. A dim label other than an entity is removed only by a layer written directly.
  • Rule 2 runs in write_layer for a layer that writes any axis or group, folding the parent's sources and the staged layer. It checks only the tuples the layer adds and those still containing a label it removes. write_layer does not refuse a later write because an ancestor left a tuple dangling.
  • Rule 4's anti-join is _living, and dead/ contains the coordinates resolve.mortal returns.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text: • A semi-join against the live labels, which the cache already has. It needs no new file, but it runs on every read, where the anti-join against a usually empty set is skipped.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text: • Whether a nested dim follows rule 1. fold_axis keys a nested dim by (period, timestep), so a parent's tombstone does not apply to its children. Removing period=2030 would tombstone (2030, t) for every t. Not built, because WorkingRecord removes no dim label and rule 2 checks no field over a nested dim.

docs.title: DEP 12: properties, metadata declared apart from data
DEP 12: properties, metadata declared apart from data
docs.text:
DEP 12 Title properties, metadata declared apart from data Author Jonas Hörsch Status Implemented (2026-10-13, steps 1 and 2) Requires DEP 10, DEP 11 Created 2026-10-12 Version Unreleased Replaces DEP 6

The design landed in the data model, the schema, the record format, the RecordLike protocol and WorkingRecord. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: Properties, which classify or describe one label of a dim, get their own section of the manifest, apart from attributes, the data. The entity-type axis becomes an Enum property of entity, whose values are categories that per-category defaults and traits key on. entity becomes a dim like any other, listed in partial, and core names neither entity nor entity_type.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Where a value is read depends on how many coordinates address it, not on what it is. p_nom and carrier both declare dims: [entity], so both land on the entity axis, and record.attributes returns neither. Widening p_nom over scenario is compatible, yet moves it to inputs/p_nom.parquet, away from the rows a layer wrote before.

The entity-type axis is a special case at every level. It is a dim plus a group into it whose rows are the entity axis file, a reserved name, and two entity-axis layouts. entity is too: always in the fold key, never broadcast, the only dim whose tombstones cascade, and the key of the read API.

The schema also cannot state a framework's per-type defaults:

Name Default per type sign 1 for Generator, Store, StorageUnit, -1 for Load, ShuntImpedance carrier "AC" for Bus, "" otherwise type "primary_energy" for GlobalConstraint, "" otherwise p_min_pu -1 for StorageUnit, 0 otherwise p_set 0 for Load, NaN otherwise

AttributeSpec.default is one value, so a tool picks one and writes the others out as data, or loses them. None of PyPSA's 142 input names differs in dtype between types, only in default.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
• A property is one value per label of its subject dim, declared under properties.<dim>, with no dims. An attribute is data and keeps dims, which may list one coordinate. The author declares which a name is.
  • One name has one spec across every section. A name declared as a property and an attribute, or as a property of two subjects, is refused. So is a property named like a dim or a group.
  • An Enum property of a dim in partial categorises its subject, and its values are categories. Trait.on and default_by may refer to it, and datarecord refuses any other property there. A dim may have several.
  • Schema.categorizing(dim) lists them. attributes_for(dim, **categories) and default_for(name, **categories) answer per label.
  • default_by maps a categorising property to per-category defaults, on properties and attributes alike. For an unset value, a read takes the first key, in declaration order, whose map lists the label's category, otherwise default. Each key categorises a dim that the value applies to, directly or through a group field. A category outside the Enum is refused. Only the default varies.
  • Trait.on is one categorising property. A trait narrows and does not grant, as DEP 16 states. An attribute that no trait claims applies to every label, and a claimed one applies to every label that some claiming trait matches. A switch is addressed by exactly the dim its trait's property categorises, and a trait with a switch must have an on.
  • A NULL on a categorised dim applies only to the labels that carry the attribute, judged by their categories at read time.
  • The fold key is exactly partial. Every dim and group broadcasts. Deletion follows DEP 11. A label is unique across types by construction, one axis row per label.
  • Record, Resolver, Fold and LayerData lose entity_types, entity_type(ctype) and entity_axis, and flags() takes no type. A per-category frame is dims[dim] filtered on a categorising column.
  • Every property of a dim is a column of dims/<dim>.parquet, NULL where the category does not have it. dims/entity_type/ goes.
  • WorkingRecord has add(dim, labels, **columns), set(attribute, value, **coords) and remove(dim, labels). add takes only columns the axis file has, and an Enum value must be a category. set takes every coordinate by keyword, a group's fields included. set writes a property, a category included, as one column of the axis row. A property keyword selects the matching labels when set runs, and nothing of the filter is stored. So set does not apply the value to a label added later. A plain NULL and default_by are the two ways to give a value to labels not yet added.
  • A category may change. Values for attributes the new category does not carry stay stored, outside every per-category read and broadcast.
  • Step 2: a property lands in dims/<dim>.parquet and every attribute in inputs/<attr>.parquet. An axis file has its labels, within keys, tombstones and properties only. record.properties[dim] returns stored values, record.attributes["p_nom"] returns long rows, and attributes_for splits into properties_for and attributes_for. Properties of a group and per-category flags are step 2 too.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
Enum makes the categories a trait or default lists checkable against a vocabulary. This settles the String-typed axis question of DEP 6: a set of categories is an Enum, or nothing keys on it. The dim must be in partial, because only a dim in partial is in the owner key and checked per label.

"Category" is used because "label" already means an axis value. A category's frame is a filter and a projection over one file. Per-type files would state each label's category twice, and Parquet stores an all-NULL chunk for almost nothing.

switch is not subsumed. A category never varies along another dim, while p_nom_extendable per investment_period does. Lifting DEP 3's restriction to the categorised dim is step 2.

The design has these costs:

  • No per-type flags, frames or applied defaults before step 2, and PyPSA's verify counts an attribute of one type as one of every type.
  • A schema keying on entity's categories must list entity in partial, or is refused.
  • Adding a carrier to an Enum carrier is a schema change.
  • A read of entity-only data goes through the fold. A static frame of forty columns is forty attribute reads and a pivot.
  • Nothing derives whether a name is metadata or data, and moving it between sections is incompatible.
  • A value per entity type alone, such as an icon, has no file keyed by category.
  • Every manifest is rewritten and every record re-exported.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
properties:
  entity:
    entity_type: { dtype: { Enum: [Bus, Generator, Load, StorageUnit] } }
    sign: { dtype: Float64, default: 1, default_by: { entity_type: { Load: -1 } } }
attributes:
  p_min_pu:
    dtype: Float64
    dims: [entity, snapshot]
    default: 0
    default_by: { entity_type: { StorageUnit: -1 } }
partial: [entity, scenario, connection]

w.add("entity", ["g1", "g2"], entity_type="Generator", carrier="wind")
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9)  # every generator, now and later
w.set("efficiency", 0.7, entity="l1", bus="b0")
w.remove("entity", ["g1"])  # tombstones g1 and its connections

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
Steps 1 and 2 landed on feat/properties-structs, with two departures:

  • partial has no rule for groups. A dim a group draws on need not be in partial, because its dead labels cover deletion.
  • A reader applies default_by through Schema.default_for, as the PyPSA tool does. record.properties and record.attributes show stored rows.

The checks: no entity or entity_type in core outside tools/, docstrings and tests. Records with and without categories differ on disk by one column. A bus_type category works like entity_type, and two categorising properties of one dim combine. set("p_max_pu", 0.9) applies to a later generator and to no bus. PyPSA round-trips sign and p_min_pu with nothing written. Widening p_nom over scenario reads old values in every scenario.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• members(dim, **categories), a per-category read with defaults applied. Deferred until a caller needs it.
  • Categories in attribute rows, to be decided. An inputs/ row would contain a categorising property, so entity NULL with entity_type = Generator applies to generators added later. It needs a specificity rule within a layer, explicit label over category row over plain NULL, with two rows of equal specificity on one label refused at staging. A read would take such a row over default_by where the row applies. flags would count it as broadcast or gain a third state. A group drawing twice on one categorised dim is refused. The decision waits for a case where layer data must apply to every label of a category, future ones included.
  • Whether a functional group over one coordinate, such as country over [bus], is a property.
  • Whether wide-frame editing returns over add, add_group and set.
  • Whether a broadcast survives materialisation. A materialised owner map stores a NULL already expanded, so set("p_max_pu", 0.9) misses a generator added in a child. A WorkingRecord's committed prefix behaves the same.
  • Whether groups edit like dims, through add(name, keys, **columns).

docs.title: DEP 13: buses and carriers are dims
DEP 13: buses and carriers are dims
docs.text:
DEP 13 Title buses and carriers are dims Author Jonas Hoersch, Bryn Pickering Status Implemented (2026-10-15) Requires DEP 12 Created 2026-10-14 Version Unreleased

The design landed in the tools reference, the schema, the data model and the record format. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: In the PyPSA tool, Bus and Carrier stop being entity types. A bus is a label of the bus dim and a carrier a label of a new carrier dim. What PyPSA stores on either becomes a property of the label or an attribute over the dim. Two core changes support this. A property may be into a dim, so that its values are that dim's labels. A property's name is scoped to its subject and addressed as subject.name.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: A bus exists twice: as a label of bus and as an entity of type Bus. Only the spelling joins the two, so remove on either leaves half behind. Because a bus is an entity, a Bus and a Load both named north collide, and every clustered pypsa-eur network has such a pair. Bus.x and Line.x are one attribute, and Bus.p cannot be written. A carrier is a string that datarecord checks against no axis. PyPSA#1474 makes buses and carriers indices in PyPSA in the same way.

docs.title: The tool
docs.text:
The PyPSA tool declares the dims entity, bus, carrier, snapshot and scenario. Its partial is entity, bus, scenario and connection.

  • entity.component replaces entity_type and categorises entity. Its Enum lists the types exported as entities, without Bus or Carrier. Shape and GlobalConstraint stay out of scope. on and default_by refer to a categorising property by its dotted name, as in sign's default_by: {entity.component: {Load: -1}}.
  • The tool places each PyPSA column by its registry entry, under PyPSA's name, following the properties rule of the data model.
PyPSA Record Bus.type, Bus.carrier, Bus.x, Bus.y, Bus.unit, Bus.location properties of bus Bus.v_nom, Bus.v_mag_pu_min, Bus.v_mag_pu_max, Bus.v_mag_pu_set attributes over bus and the dims they vary along Bus.marginal_price, Bus.v_mag_pu, Bus.v_ang results over bus and the dims they vary along Bus.p, Bus.q, Bus.control, Bus.generator, Bus.sub_network not written, because the connections determine them a custom Bus or Carrier column an attribute over its dim, as for a custom entity Carrier.color, Carrier.nice_name properties of carrier Carrier.co2_emissions, max_growth, max_relative_growth attributes over carrier a component's carrier entity.carrier, into carrier a component's sign, type properties of entity
  • partial gains bus and not carrier, so a layer restates every carrier's co2_emissions, a few dozen rows.
  • remove("bus", …) cascades as removal on any dim does, and verify reports an entity left unattached. datarecord refuses remove("carrier", …) while a stored carrier value is the label, as it does while a tuple contains a label.
  • Labels collide only within a dim. A bus and a load may share a name, and two exported types may not.
  • A custom column clashes only with an attribute. A custom Bus.country beside a custom Generator.country is country with two dims, which Requirements.columns reports. A name that a property has does not clash.
  • to_datarecord writes the two axes in PyPSA's order, adds every carrier that a component uses but n.carriers lacks, and stores "" as NULL. build rebuilds n.buses and n.carriers from them.

docs.title: A property into a dim
docs.text: PropertySpec.into is the name of a declared dim, whose labels are the property's values and whose dtype it takes. A stored value must be a live label, which datarecord checks in set, in add and in the writer, as for a group field. NULL means none. Any subject may declare one. It does not categorise, because a category is a schema Enum and labels are data. datarecord refuses a group over one coordinate into a dim, and into on a group stays for two or more coordinates. A chain is still not denormalised.

docs.title: A property's name is its subject's
docs.text:
The rule that one name has one spec still holds for attributes and results. A property is a column of its subject's file, so its name is unique there only: x on bus sits beside the attribute x. datarecord refuses at schema load:

  • a property named like its subject's key: the dim, a within parent, or a group's struct column
  • a property of a group named like one of its coordinates, which are the keywords that address a tuple
  • two names, record-wide, that differ only in case, and a . in any name.

A property is always addressed as subject.name, such as bus.carrier or entity.component. A plain name is an attribute, a result or unknown, and the error suggests the dotted forms of properties with that name. datarecord resolves the name alone, never by the keywords. Schema.resolve(name) returns the AttributeSpec or (subject, PropertySpec), and set, default_for, flags and staging call it. subject_of and property_spec(name) go. A trait bundles a property by its dotted name.

A selector keyword is bare. It is a coordinate of the attribute or a categorising property of a dim that the attribute's coordinates cover, and a coordinate comes first. carrier="gas" on co2_emissions is the dim, and component="Generator" on p_max_pu is entity.component, never the Shape attribute. add(dim, labels, **columns) takes the dim's properties bare. datarecord refuses a dotted name with kind="outputs" and in an nw.Expr. flags and the frames of properties[subject] keep plain names.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
x and y are properties and v_nom is an attribute by the properties rule, not by dtype. A coordinate describes a bus as sign describes a load, and v_nom is the per-unit base that a reinforcement layer changes.

The record-wide name rule exists so that inputs/x.parquet is one file with one value dtype. A property is a column of its subject's file, so only that column and its keywords need protecting. A prefix such as bus_x spells the subject into the name a second time, and the dot spells it once.

into on a property is the smallest way to refer to a dim's labels. It reuses the word and the live-label check of a group field, and settles the one-coordinate into question by removing the group form. A property named like its dim joins the axis on itself.

The costs: datarecord can no longer read an existing PyPSA record, so each is re-exported, as breaking changes are free. Every property set in the tool, pages and tests becomes dotted. The fold key widens by one. A round trip may add carrier rows, and a listed "" carrier comes back as none. Removing a referenced carrier takes two edits.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
w.add("bus", ["north H2"], carrier="H2", x=10.1, y=52.0)  # bare: the dim's own
w.set("bus.x", 10.2, bus="north")  # `x` alone is a Line's reactance
w.set("entity.carrier", "coal", entity="g1")  # refused: no label `coal`
w.set("carrier", "AC")  # unknown; did you mean `bus.carrier` or `entity.carrier`
w.remove("carrier", ["gas"])  # refused while an entity's carrier is `gas`

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Core: per-subject name refusals, Schema.resolve, and dotted names in set, default_for, flags and staging.
  2. Core: PropertySpec.into, with its live-label check, its remove refusal and the one-coordinate into group refused.
  3. Tool: Bus and Carrier leave the entity loop, the network source writes the two axes, and build and verify read them back.
  4. Pages, changelog and about 20 test files take the dotted names and component.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text:
• Carrier as into groups (entity_carrier, bus_carrier): two files for what one column of the label's row contains.
  • carrier as an unchecked String: no reference, "" and NULL both mean none, and removal dangles.
  • Prefixed bus columns such as bus_x, by table, registry rule or everywhere: a namespace spelled into the name, when the subject is one.
  • A plain name resolved by the call's keywords, or by the one property declared with it. A name's meaning must not depend on the other arguments, or change when another subject declares it.
  • Attributes scoped per dim too: an attribute is one file and one place in the fold key.
  • PyPSA's type renamed std_type, freeing type for the category: it keeps PyPSA's names only where convenient.
  • carrier in partial, writing Bus.p and Bus.q (p is one spec over connection), and bus.type as an Enum (it is free text in PyPSA).

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• Whether a property into a partial dim, such as entity.carrier, may categorise.
  • Whether a default such as bus.carrier: AC must be a live label. datarecord never checks a default.
  • Whether bus is worth its fold-key column, measured on a pypsa-eur-sized record.
  • Whether a custom bus column can be a property, which would remove the one remaining custom-column clash.
  • Whether selector keywords need a qualified form, for a categorising name on two dims that one attribute's coordinates cover.
  • What PyPSA#1474 lands as: an unlisted carrier may become an error, and "" may stop meaning none.

docs.title: DEP 14: combining a record with an extension
DEP 14: combining a record with an extension
docs.text: DEP 14 Title combining a record with an extension Author Jonas Hörsch, Bryn Pickering Status Rejected (2026-10-20) Requires DEP 12, DEP 13 Created 2026-10-14

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: combine(base, extension, con) presents a tool's record and the data a reader derives beside it as one lazy RecordLike under one united schema. You read it directly or write it as one record. The extension adds names and never redefines one. The idea and its first prototype are Bryn Pickering's, in PR #56, and this DEP redesigns it against the current RecordLike.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A PyPSA-Eur workflow exports its network with PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, ws.con), under the tool's schema. Beside it, the workflow has data that PyPSA does not model, keyed by the same entities, buses and periods. Examples are custom constraints, a country per bus and an emission intensity per generator. There is no correct way to put both in one record:

  • A layer declares nothing. A record has one schema, so datarecord refuses w.set("co2_intensity", …) as undeclared.
  • A hand-written union is unchecked. A child layer under a wider schema widens the manifest, but datarecord checks only compatibility. That check lets the union change a base default or unit, or widen a base Enum.
  • A layer cannot add a property on a shared subject. Per label, the fold keeps the deepest axis row whole, so a child that adds bus.country must restate every base property of each bus.
  • A standalone directory is one source with one schema.

docs.title: Uniting the schemas
docs.text:
base.schema.extended_by(extension.schema) -> Schema returns the united schema, or raises ValueError naming the entry and the rule:

Entry The extension may add A shared entry must Refused dim a new dim, within any dim be identical a differing re-declaration group a new group, over and into any dims be identical a differing re-declaration property subject.name a new name, on a new or a shared subject be identical a differing re-declaration attribute, result a new name, over any dims and groups be identical a differing re-declaration trait a new trait, on any categorising property be identical attributes or switch listing a name the base declares partial its new dims and groups not applicable a shared dim or group the base's partial lacks meta key a new key have an equal value a differing value

Identical means equal as declared, unit, default and default_by included. Re-declaring keeps an extension's schema valid alone: a trait on entity.component needs the entity dim, the entity.component property and entity in partial. version is the base's and is not compared. The united schema then passes Schema's own validator.

Every base name keeps its spec and every base category has what it had, so extended_by(...).compatible_with(base) is always empty.

docs.title: The combined record
docs.text:
combine computes the united schema. It refuses an extension with rows of an attribute or result the base declares, both at the call and from the mapping keys alone. Every frame is planned on con through as_relation, so datarecord refuses a relation from another connection and collects nothing.

  • dims and groups are a union by key: the base's keys in its order, then the extension's new keys in its order.
  • properties[s] is joined per subject over the united keys. A base-declared column comes from the base for its keys and from the extension for keys only the extension has. An extension-added column comes from the extension, and anything else is NULL.
  • attributes and outputs are taken by name, each from one side unchanged.
  • flags(**categories) is computed from the combined frames against the united schema, by the protocol's definition.

combine is a read-time view. It folds nothing and removes nothing, and takes any RecordLike on either side: a tool's record, a Record, a WorkingRecord or another combination. Written, it becomes an ordinary record, by ws.write(combine(...), uri), store.root(...) or rev.child(combine(rev.record, ext, con)). Because of the invariant, compatible_with accepts the manifest widening of the last. A combination is not a Record, so you edit it after writing it.

FrameRecord(schema, dims=, properties=, groups=, attributes=, outputs=) is an extension's shape: native frames of any backend narwhals reads. A subject with properties and no dims frame takes its labels from the properties' key, and a declared column that a frame lacks is NULL.

combine and FrameRecord live in core as datarecord/combine.py, and extended_by lives in schema.py beside compatible_with.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
Under this rule, datarecord refuses any change to the base, not only a clash with its names. A new trait that claims p_nom for generators collides with nothing, yet takes it from every other entity, because a trait narrows. Identity on shared entries, with new traits that claim only new names, makes the invariant hold. A tool then reads a combined record's base names as it reads its own record.

combine divides subjects by key and attributes by name. An axis or group row is keyed by one label, so the two sides meet on it. Attribute rows overlap through the broadcast rule, and dividing them between sources is the fold, which is a layer's job. For the same reason, combine ignores an extension's value for a base column on a base key. Changing a base value is a layer's job.

The costs: flags is a scan per call, where a Record's is free. An extension may add labels to a shared axis, so a mistyped label becomes a new one. An extension that disagrees with the base on a base key goes unnoticed. Re-declaring shared entries makes an extension verbose.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
base = PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, ws.con)
s = base.schema
schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": s.dimensions["entity"],
        "bus": s.dimensions["bus"],
        "period": s.dimensions["period"],
        "limit": Dimension(dtype=nw.String()),
    },
    properties={
        "entity": {"component": s.properties["entity"]["component"]},
        "bus": {"country": PropertySpec(dtype=nw.String())},
    },
    attributes={
        "limit_constant": AttributeSpec(dtype=nw.Float64(), dims={"limit", "period"}),
        "co2_intensity": AttributeSpec(dtype=nw.Float64(), dims={"entity"}),
    },
    traits={
        "emitting": Trait(
            attributes={"co2_intensity"}, on={"entity.component": {"Generator", "Link"}}
        )
    },
    partial={"entity"},
)
extension = FrameRecord(
    schema,
    properties={"bus": countries},  # bus | country
    attributes={"limit_constant": limits, "co2_intensity": intensities},
)
record = combine(base, extension, ws.con)
record.flags(component="Generator")["co2_intensity"]
ws.write(record, "resources/networks/base_s_37.record")

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Schema.extended_by, a parametrised test per refused row, and a test that compatible_with(base) is empty.
  2. combine's members over con, ordered by numbering each side's rows and sorting outermost.
  3. The frames-based flags, sharing categorized_dim, selected and attributes_among with the fold's.
  4. FrameRecord, exported with combine from datarecord.
  5. Pages, usage pages and changelog.

Checks: reading every member of a combination over frames that raise on collect runs no query. Projected to base names and keys, every combined frame equals the base's. flags(component="Bus") lacks co2_intensity.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text:
• An extension layer, which declares its own schema additions or is written under a hand-united schema. The first is the layered schema that datarecord rejects by having one schema per record. Both need a tree, cannot be read before they are written, and restate the base properties of every shared subject.
  • The prototype's eager widening, which collected both sides to pyarrow and broke lazy Frames.
  • Refusing only colliding trait names, which lets a new trait narrow base attributes.
  • Taking flags from the sides. The extension has no category data, and the PyPSA tool's record returns {}.
  • Merging two sides' rows of one attribute. Dividing overlapping rows is a fold.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• Data checks on shared subjects: whether datarecord should refuse extension-only labels on a shared axis, or disagreement on a base key. Either check reads both frames, perhaps in the writer.
  • Relaxed identity: whether the extension may widen a base Enum, or add a trait without on that bundles base names.
  • Adding an extension to an existing tree without restating the base, which needs axis rows folded per column.

docs.title: DEP 15: a dim is flat
docs.text:
DEP 15 Title a dim is flat Author Jonas Hoersch Status Implemented (2026-10-20) Requires DEP 13 Created 2026-10-19 Version Unreleased

The design landed in the schema, the data model, the fold and the tools reference. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: Dimension.within leaves core, so every dim is one label set, keyed by its label alone. A label scoped to a parent becomes a label unique across its dim, plus a property into the parent, such as snapshot.period. DEP 13 added this reference. A chain is a chain of such properties, and several parents are several properties.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A multi-period PyPSA network declares snapshot within period, and every place that touches the snapshot axis has to handle it:

  • Every series carries its period. Every input and result over snapshot is over period too, so p_max_pu is keyed by (entity, period, snapshot). A NULL period is then a second way of addressing a snapshot.
  • Checks skip a nested dim. remove and the writer do not check a property into one, or a group field over one, and remove does not cascade to its tuples. The trait check passes over a nested partial dim, and set("dim.name", mapping) refuses one.
  • Two bugs follow. datarecord accepts an attribute over a nested dim without its parent, so its rows match no point. A pointwise set with a NULL period drops the rest of the series.
  • The framework has no nested dims. In math-spec, the model-spec language datarecord feeds, every dimension has one list of labels. A multi-period snapshot there is one flat dim with a snapshot → period relation. Its guidance states that two dependent dimensions, declared as a product cut back by a mask, are one relation. A tool that feeds it flattens the (period, snapshot) key anyway.

docs.title: One key column
docs.text:
Dimension has dtype, unit and description. A dim's key is its label: dims/<dim>.parquet is keyed by the one column <dim>, and record.dims[dim] is that column. Its labels are unique across the dim. datarecord refuses a manifest that declares within at load, and the error names the property into the parent that replaces it.

A label scoped per parent becomes a flat label and a property into the parent. The source picks the labels, which need only be unique across the dim. Where the point's name inside its parent matters, it is a further property.

Declared before Declared under this DEP timestep within period snapshot, snapshot.period into period, snapshot.timestep timestep in period in horizon snapshot.period into period, period.horizon into horizon timestep within {period, stage} snapshot.period into period, snapshot.stage into stage

A chain is not denormalised, as for any classification. snapshot has no horizon column, and the horizon is a join through period.

A selector keyword selects by a parent. The keyword is bare and matches any property of a dim that the attribute's coordinates cover. period=2030 on p_max_pu selects the snapshots whose snapshot.period is 2030, and timestep=t0 the snapshot at t0 in every period. datarecord still refuses a keyword when two such dims both declare period.

docs.title: What loses its special case
docs.text: Where Before, for a nested dim Under this DEP axis key, record.dims[dim] (*parents, dim), Schema.axis_key dim axis fold, dead labels keyed by the parents too by the label broadcast a series has its parent, and a NULL parent means every period a NULL dim means every label add(dim, …) parent keys required properties only set("dim.name", mapping) refused as on any dim remove, the writer no into check, no group cascade, no field check every dim label and trait check on set skipped for a partial dim every partial dim property names none named like a within parent snapshot.period allowed versioning changing within incompatible the entry goes

docs.title: The PyPSA tool
docs.text:
• A single-period network's schema is unchanged.
  • A multi-period network's snapshot is flat. Its label is PyPSA's timestep where the timesteps are unique across periods, and an integer position otherwise.
  • snapshot.period is into period. The tool declares snapshot.timestep only beside positions, because a timestep label already contains it.
  • Inputs and results over snapshot are no longer over period. period_weighting_objective and _years stay over period.
  • build rebuilds the snapshot MultiIndex in axis order from snapshot.period and the label or snapshot.timestep.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The scoping comes from how the source picks its labels, not from the axis. t1 identifies no snapshot alone because PyPSA reuses it per period, and a source that numbers its snapshots once has no nesting to declare. A property records the same relation in the one form that datarecord already checks, folds and selects on. A reader then reads snapshot.period as it reads bus.carrier.

With one key column, datarecord needs one rule. The axis key, the fold key and the broadcast rule each had a branch for (*parents, dim). Every check that could not place a label by one column skipped it. Removing the shape removes the skips. The bugs above become unrepresentable. When no dim has a parent, no attribute omits one and no series leaves one NULL.

into can now express timestep. The distinction between within and into held because within scoped a label set and into could not. With a flat label set, the snapshot is a classification like any other, and each snapshot has one period.

The NULL-parent set bug is narrower than within. It is a fold bug with any two dims outside partial, which within made routine by putting a second such dim on every series. The bug goes from the snapshot and stays for other schemas.

The costs: a source whose inner labels repeat across parents must make unique ones. datarecord can no longer read a record that declares within, so each is re-exported, as breaking changes are free. "The same timestep in every period" is no longer one row with a NULL period. It is a selector over snapshot.timestep, which stages one row per matching snapshot. To get (period, timestep) per row, a reader joins the snapshot's properties.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": Dimension(dtype=nw.String()),
        "period": Dimension(dtype=nw.Int64()),
        "snapshot": Dimension(dtype=nw.Int64()),
    },
    properties={
        "snapshot": {
            "period": PropertySpec(into="period"),
            "timestep": PropertySpec(dtype=nw.Datetime("us")),
        }
    },
    attributes={
        "p_max_pu": AttributeSpec(dtype=nw.Float64(), dims={"entity", "snapshot"})
    },
)

w.add("period", [2030, 2040])
w.add(
    "snapshot", [0, 1, 2, 3], period=[2030, 2030, 2040, 2040], timestep=[t0, t1, t0, t1]
)
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.8, entity="g1", period=2030)  # snapshots 0 and 1
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.5, entity="g1", timestep=t0)  # snapshots 0 and 2
w.set("snapshot.period", {3: 2030})  # was refused on a nested dim
w.remove("period", [2040])  # refused while a snapshot.period is 2040

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Schema: Dimension.within, its validation, _ancestors and axis_key go, and callers key by the dim. A within in a manifest is refused with into named. The property-name and versioning rules lose within.
  2. Read: the axis fold, dead labels and the dims and properties frames are keyed by the label.
  3. Writer: an axis file's columns are the dim and its properties. Every into property and group field is checked against live labels.
  4. WorkingRecord: add without parent keys, set on any dim's property, and remove's cascade, into refusal, trait check and staging keys over every dim.
  5. Tool: a flat snapshot with snapshot.period and snapshot.timestep, series over snapshot alone, and build from the properties.
  6. Pages, usage pages, changelog and tests. The links of DEP 12 and DEP 13 to the removed within anchors are retargeted, which revises no argument.

Checks: no within or axis_key in src/. A multi-period network with repeating timesteps and one with unique ones round-trip. remove and the writer both refuse remove("period", …) while a snapshot's snapshot.period is the label. A manifest that declares within is refused with into named.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text:
• A group over (period, timestep) as the snapshot: a masked product, which math-spec's guidance rejects, and a struct-valued key in every time series.
  • within kept beside the property: two spellings of one relation, and every special case above stays for the one that keeps it.
  • Composite string labels as a rule ("2030|t1"): the source picks its labels, and a rule would make datarecord parse them.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• Whether Schema should offer a helper that declares a dim with its parent property in one call.
  • Whether the selector needs a qualified form when two dims that the attribute's coordinates cover declare period.
  • The NULL-parent pointwise set bug, for schemas with two dims outside partial.

docs.title: DEP 16: remove traits
docs.text:
DEP 16 Title remove traits Author Jonas Hoersch Status Implemented (2026-10-20) Created 2026-10-20 Version Unreleased Replaces DEP 1 (its traits), DEP 3 (switches)

The design landed in the schema, the data model and the tools reference. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: Trait leaves the schema, together with its manifest form and every rule that reads it. An attribute applies to every label its dims address, and a property to every label of its subject. Categories and default_by stay. A tool that needs a per-type vocabulary keeps it itself.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A trait narrows which labels of a categorised dim have an attribute or property. That one rule touches much of the code:

  • On the read path, a NULL over a categorised dim expands only to the labels that have the attribute. categories.carriers builds a (label, attribute) relation per category combination for this.
  • flags(**categories) drops the attributes that a category does not have.
  • set refuses a value on a label whose category does not have the attribute.
  • Compatibility compares every category of two schemas in Schema._dropped_by_category.
  • datarecord declares and validates switch, and nothing reads it.
  • _check_trait checks six rules on on, the bundle and the switch.

One reader uses traits: the PyPSA tool. It derives one trait per component type from PyPSA's registry, and asks attributes_for which attributes a type takes. That answer is PyPSA's, read back from a schema the tool wrote. datarecord stores it, folds by it and validates against it, for a vocabulary that datarecord never defines. The queryable vocabulary that traits were meant to give, such as everything investable, has no caller.

docs.title: What goes
docs.text: Construct Becomes Trait, Schema.traits, traits: in a manifest removed, and datarecord refuses a manifest that declares traits at load Trait.switch removed, and the switch attribute stays an ordinary attribute Schema.attributes_for(dim, **categories) removed, in favour of [a for a in schema.attributes if schema.addresses(a, dim)] Schema.properties_for(subject, **categories) removed, in favour of schema.properties[subject] narrowed broadcast (categories.carriers) a NULL means every label of the dim flags(**categories) filtering by carried attribute only the rows that apply to a matching label count set refusing a label whose category lacks it removed, and the label check stays _dropped_by_category in compatibility removed

docs.title: What stays
docs.text:
• An Enum property of a partial dim still categorises it. Schema.categorizing, require_categorizing and require_listed stay.
  • default_by keys on a categorising property, and default_for(name, **categories) is unchanged. It never depended on traits.
  • partial is unchanged. It was a condition for a category, not an input to a trait.
  • flags(ctype="Generator") and a property keyword in set select labels by category.
  • with_defaults applies default_for per category combination. Every name now applies to every label, so its _carries_ columns go.

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
traits is no field of Schema, and extra="forbid" would refuse it with a generic message. A mode="before" validator refuses it first, as for within:

a schema takes no `traits`: an attribute reaches every label its `dims`
address; scope a value with a category keyword on `set`, and keep a
per-type vocabulary in the tool that needs it

docs.title: The PyPSA tool
docs.text:
• _registry_schema declares no traits. It keeps the per-type input names as a cached _carried(ctype).
  • _NetworkSource.schema adds a type's custom columns to that map, not to a trait.
  • _verify and build call _carried(ctype) where they called attributes_for(ENTITY, ctype=ctype).
  • The static frame contains the entity properties that _carried(ctype) lists, where it called carried_properties.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The tool already has the narrowing. PyPSA's registry already lists which attributes a Load takes. A copy in the schema makes datarecord enforce a framework's vocabulary, and under the package layout framework knowledge stays out of core.

A broadcast over every label is the general rule. Every dim that is not categorised already broadcasts that way. A categorised dim was the one exception, and the fold, flags and validation each had a branch for it.

default_by is not a trait. It sets a value per category, and has no effect on whether a value exists, so it stays unchanged.

The costs: set("p_max_pu", 0.9) now also applies to loads, which PyPSA ignores. datarecord no longer refuses a misplaced value on write. A NULL row expands over every label in the owner map, not only the labels that had the attribute. Every record that declares traits is re-exported, as breaking changes are free.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Before:

Schema(
    ...,
    traits={
        "dispatchable": Trait(
            attributes={"p_max_pu"},
            on={"entity.ctype": {"Generator", "StorageUnit"}},
        )
    },
)
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9)  # every generator and storage unit, never a load
schema.attributes_for("entity", ctype="Load")  # no p_max_pu

After:

Schema(...)  # no traits
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9, ctype=["Generator", "StorageUnit"])  # one row per label
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9)  # every entity; PyPSA never reads a load's value
schema.default_for("p_min_pu", ctype="StorageUnit")  # -1, as before

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. schema.py: Trait, Schema.traits, _check_trait, attributes_for, properties_for, _carried and _dropped_by_category go. A traits key is refused at load.
  2. __init__.py: Trait leaves the exports.
  3. layered/categories.py: narrowed, label_carriers, carriers, attributes_among and carried_properties go, and with_defaults loses _carries_.
  4. layered/resolve.py: the carriers join in the broadcast goes.
  5. layered/fold.py: flags(**categories) filters by matching labels only.
  6. mutable.py: the category check in set goes.
  7. tools/pypsa.py: as in the PyPSA tool. BY_CTYPE stays for default_by.
  8. Tests: the trait tests are deleted, and fixtures.py declares no traits.
  9. Pages, usage pages and CHANGELOG.md drop traits and switch.
  10. DEP 1 and DEP 3 take Superseded-By this DEP.

Checks: no trait in src/. A manifest with traits is refused with the replacement named. A PyPSA network round-trips.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text:
• Traits kept as an unenforced bundle for dispatch: a vocabulary that no caller asks for.
  • Narrowing moved onto AttributeSpec as carried_by: the same rule under another name, with every branch kept.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• What build does with a value that its type does not take. The recommendation is that _verify reports it, as for an unknown type, and does not raise.
  • Whether a category still needs partial, which existed for per-label narrowing. The recommendation is to keep it, because default_by per label needs a dim that the owner map keys per label.
  • The committable case that DEP 3 raised. The recommendation is to leave it to the reader of the committable attribute.
  • Owner-map size. The recommendation is to measure the PyPSA example before and after, and change nothing unless it regresses.

docs.title: DEP 17: results are attributes
docs.text:
DEP 17 Title results are attributes Author Jonas Hoersch Status Implemented (2026-10-20) Requires DEP 16 Created 2026-10-20 Version Unreleased Superseded-By DEP 20 (its SubNetwork as an entity, and its tombstones)

The design landed in the schema, the record format, the record, the fold and the tools reference. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: A result becomes an ordinary attribute. A layer has one attributes/ directory, and inputs/ and outputs/ go, with Schema.results, RecordLike.outputs, Kind and every kind="outputs". Only a tool knows which attributes it computes, and Tool.results gives way to to_datarecord(model, con, results_only=True, base=record).

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A record has two vocabularies of one shape. attributes and results are both mappings of AttributeSpec, and each lands in its own directory, inputs/ or outputs/. The split touches every part of the code:

  • Schema.results is a second mapping, and the name check, spec, the column check and compatibility each take the union of the two.
  • RecordLike.outputs sits beside attributes, and LayerData.attributes(kind) and attribute(name, kind) take a Kind.
  • On the read path, outputs/ does not overlay. A revision reads its own layer only, so a child loses its parent's results.
  • set(..., kind="outputs") checks the name against results, skips the label check and keeps staged results apart.
  • The writer checks a result's shape only for attribute, breakpoint and value.
  • The owner map is keyed by a kind that is always inputs.

A framework draws the distinction. PyPSA marks an attribute "Output" in its registry, and datarecord stores, validates and resolves that mark for a vocabulary it never defines. To read a solved marginal_price, you must also know which of two mappings has it.

docs.title: What goes
docs.text: Before Under this DEP inputs/<attr>.parquet, outputs/<attr>.parquet attributes/<attr>.parquet, one directory per layer Schema.results removed: Schema.attributes declares a result the name check across attributes and results one name, one entry in attributes Schema.spec reading attributes, then results attributes alone results in compatibility removed: attributes versions as before RecordLike.outputs, Record.outputs removed: record.attributes[name] Kind, attributes(kind), attribute(name, kind) attributes(), attribute(name) the read path's outputs removed: a result overlays like any attribute, and a read returns the latest layer's row owner maps keyed by kind one owner map: owner_map_uri(id), owner_map_<id> set(..., kind="outputs") set(name, frame), with the attribute check of set the label exemption for a result removed: every label must resolve staged_outputs_<attr>_<id> the staged attribute table the writer's shape exemption for a result removed: a result's file has its declared coordinates outputs/ written only when non-empty removed: attributes/ contains what the source has Tool.results(model, con) to_datarecord(model, con, results_only=True, base=record)

docs.title: Loading an old layer
docs.text:
When a source opens a layer with an inputs/ or outputs/ directory, datarecord refuses it:

layer <id> has an `inputs/` directory; a layer contains every attribute in
`attributes/`, results included. Re-export the record.

docs.title: The tool interface
docs.text:
Tool.results goes, and to_datarecord takes results_only and base:

def to_datarecord(
    self,
    model: Any,
    con: DuckDBPyConnection,
    *,
    results_only: bool = False,
    base: RecordLike | None = None,
) -> RecordLike: ...

base is the record the model was built from. It is required with results_only=True and refused otherwise.

With results_only=True, to_datarecord presents only what the solve produced: the result attributes and the intermediate results they need. The tool writes this thin layer as a child of the record the model was built from, rev.child(layer), without staging it through a WorkingRecord. Where inputs were edited first, their edits are committed as a child, and the thin layer goes on top of that child.

docs.title: Intermediate results
docs.text:
A solve derives structure as well as values, such as PyPSA's SubNetworks or a cycle matrix. Each is an ordinary dim, entity or attribute that the tool writes and its schema declares. A SubNetwork is an entity with ctype="SubNetwork", and a line's sub_network is an attribute whose value is one such entity. A cycle matrix is an attribute over a cycle dim and the lines.

On every results_only write the tool replaces them. The model does not record what the base had, so the tool reads the intermediate entities and labels in base, such as its SubNetwork entities. The thin layer tombstones those it does not write again, then adds the new ones. A re-solve that numbers SubNetworks differently leaves no stale label behind.

docs.title: The PyPSA tool
docs.text:
• _output_attributes(c) still reads PyPSA's registry status "Output", and _result_attributes still maps each output to its record name.
  • _registry_schema adds the outputs to attributes. A name that is an input on another type stays dropped.
  • build copies every attribute the record has into the network, so a solved bus's marginal_price arrives as any attribute does.
  • The tool reads "Output" only on import, to decide what results_only presents. It never drops data from build or from a full export.
  • to_datarecord writes outputs as attributes, so a solved network round-trips its results through attributes/.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
A result already has a dtype, dims and a description, and its file already has the long schema. Keeping it apart needs a branch in every reader, and gives only the overlay rule in return.

A child inherits its parent's results. A child that changes nothing a solve reads keeps its parent's solution. A child that changes inputs has results computed from its parent, which is the staleness a staged result already has after an input edit.

Only the tool deals with "output". PyPSA's registry already lists which attributes a solve fills, and only the tool's import reads that. This follows the package layout, under which framework knowledge stays out of core.

A full export and a results layer differ only in what they present. With one to_datarecord, the rule for each result sits in one place.

Every row of a record sets only declared labels, so a reader that joins a result to dims["entity"] never finds an orphan.

The costs: every record is re-exported, as breaking changes are free. A child of a solved revision shows results that its inputs no longer support. datarecord validates a results layer in full, so it must contain the labels that its results set.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Before:

n = PyPSA.build(w)
n.optimize()
for attr, frame in PyPSA.results(n, w.con).items():
    w.set(attr, frame, kind="outputs")
solved = rev.child(w.edits)  # inputs and results in one layer
solved.record.outputs["marginal_price"]  # a child of solved has none

After:

inputs = rev.child(w.edits)
n = PyPSA.build(inputs.record)
n.optimize()
solved = inputs.child(
    PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, w.con, results_only=True, base=inputs.record)
)
solved.record.attributes["marginal_price"]  # a child of solved reads it too
PyPSA.build(solved.record)  # marginal_price is in the network

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. schema.py: results and its name, column and compatibility branches go, and spec reads attributes.
  2. record.py: Kind and outputs go, and attributes() and attribute(name) lose kind.
  3. layered/sources.py reads attributes/ and refuses a layer with inputs/ or outputs/.
  4. layered/resolve.py: _outputs goes, and map_kinds becomes one fold without a kind parameter.
  5. store.py: owner_map_uri(id) drops kind.
  6. layered/record.py: outputs goes.
  7. layered/write.py writes attributes/, and the outputs branch and the result exemptions go.
  8. mutable.py: kind on set, _validate_result, outputs and the staged outputs tables go.
  9. tools/base.py: results goes, and to_datarecord takes results_only and base.
  10. tools/pypsa.py: results folds into to_datarecord, which replaces the intermediates in base.
  11. Tests of kind="outputs" and outputs are rewritten or deleted, and fixtures.py declares results as attributes.
  12. Pages, usage pages and CHANGELOG.md.

Checks: no outputs, Kind or results field in src/. An old layer is refused with attributes/ named. A solved PyPSA network round-trips with its results, and a child reads its parent's results. A re-solve leaves no stale SubNetwork. results_only without base, or base without it, is refused.

docs.title: Rejected ideas
docs.text:
• A result: bool flag on AttributeSpec: the split again under another name, and still a framework's vocabulary.
  • outputs/ kept beside attributes/: two directories for one shape, and every reader still branching.
  • build skipping outputs: it would drop data the record has, and a solved record would build unsolved.
  • A PyPSA.attach(n, w) that stages results: a thin layer from to_datarecord writes them without a WorkingRecord.

docs.title: Open issues
docs.text:
• Stale results after an input edit. Results now inherit, so the open question on staged results widens. The recommendation is that the caller, not datarecord, keeps results consistent with their inputs.
  • Detecting intermediates that no longer fit their inputs. This needs provenance of which inputs each came from, and is deferred.
  • Filtering a record before build, such as one period or chosen outputs. This is a separate feature, not designed here.

docs.title: DEP 18: drop narwhals
docs.text:
DEP 18 Title drop narwhals Author Jonas Hoersch Status Implemented (2026-10-20) Requires DEP 17 Created 2026-10-20 Version Unreleased

The design landed in the schema, the record, editing, the format and tools. Where they and this DEP differ, follow those pages.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: datarecord drops narwhals from core and tools, and DuckDB is the one query engine. A record returns bare DuckDBPyRelations, and the write path takes relations and pandas, polars or arrow frames. Dtypes are mathspec's DimensionDtype and ParameterDtype, stored as plain strings, with one fixed DuckDB type map. A dim may list its labels with one_of: [...]. A property may take its labels from a dim with one_of: <dim>, which replaces into.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Every record is DuckDB underneath, and narwhals wraps it between DuckDB and the caller:

  • Record wraps a relation with nw.from_native, and a caller who wants SQL unwraps it with to_native().
  • set turns any frame into narwhals and then into a relation: two conversions for one DuckDB scan.
  • duck.py imports private narwhals modules for its type translation, so datarecord pins narwhals to >=2,<3,!=2.21.0.
  • The manifest stores narwhals names such as "Float64", and a mathspec model declares float and a dimension's one_of, so every reader translates.
  • Nothing downstream distinguishes Date, number widths or time zones.
  • tools/base.to_relation exists because narwhals has no PIVOT.

narwhals takes 175 lines in 9 files under src/, and 219 lines in 13 test files.

docs.title: mathspec
docs.text: datarecord pins mathspec at 8982c556114992d149a83b3c6f3604c72e569829, the merge of energy-models/mathspec#915. There a dimension may write one_of: [labels] beside dtype: str, and dtype defaults to str. DimensionDtype is float, int, str or datetime, and ParameterDtype is float, int, bool or str. Before a release, the pin moves to the merged commit.

docs.title: Dtypes
docs.text:
Declaration DuckDB type dtype: float DOUBLE dtype: int BIGINT dtype: bool BOOLEAN dtype: str VARCHAR dtype: datetime TIMESTAMP (no time zone) dtype: str, one_of: [labels] ENUM of the labels one_of: <dim> that dim's type

A dim takes every dtype but bool, and attributes and properties take every dtype but datetime. Only a dim lists labels, and only a property takes one_of: <dim>. An attribute takes no one_of, as a mathspec parameter takes none. The map is one constant in duck.py, read wherever a column is typed. Date, Int32, Float32 and time zones go.

A dim that lists its labels has an ENUM column, and add refuses a label outside the list, naming the list. Only a str dim lists its labels, as in mathspec.

A property with one_of: <dim> takes its labels from that dim and declares no dtype. Its column has the dim's type: an ENUM where the dim lists its labels, and TIMESTAMP for a datetime dim. A stored value that is not NULL is a live label, checked where into was checked. The property may be of a dim or a group. mathspec#915 refuses a dimension reference on a parameter, but a datarecord property is a mathspec relation column.

Struct columns are derived and never declared. A group's column is a STRUCT with a field per key coordinate, typed as its dim. An owner flag is a STRUCT of BOOLEAN. The fixed columns stay fixed: attribute VARCHAR, breakpoint DOUBLE, deleted BOOLEAN and breakpoints BOOLEAN.

docs.title: into goes
docs.text:
PropertySpec.into and GroupSpec.into are removed. bus.country into country becomes bus.country: {one_of: country}. A group over [bus, scenario] into country becomes a property country: {one_of: country} of that group. A group loses two things that into gave it:

  • exactly one label per tuple, because the property may be NULL
  • a column named after the dim, because the property's name is free and country is a convention.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Schema.categorizing(dim) picks the properties of a dim in partial that are {one_of: <d>}, where d lists its labels. A property one_of a dim that lists no labels does not categorise, because its labels are data that a layer adds and removes.

PyPSA's ctype becomes a dim {dtype: str, one_of: [Generator, Line, ...]}, and entity.ctype becomes {one_of: ctype}. connection.role becomes {one_of: role} on a dim role that lists input, output and attached.

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
A dtype is written as its mathspec string, "dtype": "float", and one_of as in the table above. An old manifest fails at load, and the error names the replacement:

dimension 'snapshot' declares dtype {"Datetime": "us"}, a narwhals name;
write "datetime" (one of float, int, str, datetime)
