Workspace.at(uri) reads a standalone directory as a fold over one layer, whose layout is a layer's.

Reading a directory as a fold over one layer The directory out contains manifest.json, dims and attributes, the layout of one layer. Read with ws.at, it is a fold over that one layer, so the owner map assigns every key to that layer. out/ manifest.json, dims/, attributes/ owner map entity scenario layer gas NULL out wind NULL out ws.at("out/") a fold over one layer

The owner map assigns every key to the one layer, the axis order is each file's row order, and partial has no effect. One Record reads both a directory and a revision, so a reader cannot tell them apart. store.layer(id) reads one layer of a store alone in the same way.

See also

One interface over a directory and a tree gives the reasons for one Record. The store page describes Workspace.at and Workspace.write.

docs.title: The schema
docs.text:
This page describes every key a schema accepts, in the order a schema declares them, and what datarecord refuses at load. A schema is the Schema of a record: the dims, properties, attributes and partial that may exist, with their dtypes. The data model defines each of those words.

The running example declares this schema:

from datarecord import AttributeSpec, Dimension, PropertySpec, Schema

schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": Dimension(),
        "bus": Dimension(),
        "carrier": Dimension(),
        "snapshot": Dimension(dtype="int"),
        "ctype": Dimension(one_of=["Generator", "Link", "Load"]),
        "connection": Dimension(over=["entity", "bus"]),
    },
    attributes={
        "p_nom": AttributeSpec(dtype="float", dims={"entity"}, default=0.0, unit="MW"),
        "efficiency": AttributeSpec(dtype="float", dims={"connection"}, default=1.0),
        "p_max_pu": AttributeSpec(
            dtype="float",
            dims={"entity", "snapshot"},
            default=1.0,
            default_by={"entity.ctype": {"Load": 0.0}},
        ),
    },
    properties={
        "entity": {
            "ctype": PropertySpec(one_of="ctype"),
            "carrier": PropertySpec(one_of="carrier"),
        },
    },
    partial={"entity", "bus", "connection"},
)

Schema.default_for("p_max_pu", ctype="Load") returns 0.0, and Schema.default_for("p_max_pu") returns 1.0.

A Schema and each spec are frozen pydantic models that refuse an undeclared key. Every refusal on this page raises when the schema is built or read from a manifest.

docs.title: version
docs.text: version is an integer, 1 by default, that you raise with each change to the declarations. datarecord stores it and compares nothing against it. Compatibility lists the changes a child revision's schema may make.

docs.title: dimensions
docs.text:
dimensions maps each dim's name to a Dimension, multi-dims among them.

Key Value Default over a multi-dim's coordinates, each mapped to the dim it draws on None dtype "float", "int", "str" or "datetime" "str" one_of the dim's labels, in order None unit what the labels measure None description what the dim is, in prose None

A schema that declares attributes declares at least one dim, because attribute data over no dim is no record.

docs.title: over
docs.text: over declares a multi-dim. A list is short for the dict whose keys equal its values, so over=["entity", "bus"] is over={"entity": "entity", "bus": "bus"}. The keys are the coordinate names, in field order, and Schema.over("connection") returns them. datarecord refuses a multi-dim that also declares dtype or one_of, and a coordinate that draws on an undeclared dim or on a multi-dim.

docs.title: one_of
docs.text: one_of declares a dim with one_of, whose axis is the list. Only a "str" dim takes it. datarecord refuses an empty list, a label listed twice, and one_of on any other dtype.

docs.title: attributes
docs.text:
attributes maps each attribute's name to an AttributeSpec. One name is one spec, one file and one value dtype, record-wide.

Key Value Default dtype "float", "int", "bool" or "str" required dims the dims and multi-dims that address a value frozenset() default the value at a point no row covers None default_by a default per category, which overrides default {} breakpoints whether a row may have a piecewise-linear curve False unit what the values measure None description what the attribute is, in prose None

datarecord refuses a dims entry that is not a declared dim. It also refuses a multi-dim in dims beside a dim named like one of its coordinates, such as {"connection", "bus"}.

docs.title: default_by
docs.text:
default_by maps a categorising property, written subject.name, to a map from category to default. At a label whose category a map lists, the first key in declaration order gives the default. Elsewhere default applies. Schema.default_for(name, **categories) returns the default for an attribute or a subject.name property, taking each category by the property's plain name.

datarecord refuses a key that is not a categorising property, naming the reason:

attribute 'p_nom''s `default_by` is keyed by 'entity.carrier', which refers to 'carrier', but 'carrier' is not a one_of dim

It also refuses a category that the referred dim's one_of does not list. It refuses a key on a dim that the attribute or property is not indexed over. A property is indexed over its subject and the dims that the subject's coordinates draw on.

docs.title: properties
docs.text:
properties maps each subject dim to a map from property name to PropertySpec.

Key Value Default dtype "float", "int", "bool" or "str" None one_of the dim the property refers to None default the value for a label no layer wrote one for None default_by a default per category, as on an attribute {} unit what the values measure None description what the property is, in prose None

A property declares exactly one of dtype and one_of. With one_of, the property refers to that dim and takes its type. Schema.resolve("entity.carrier") returns the subject and the spec, and Schema.categorizing(dim) lists the categorising properties of dim.

datarecord refuses a property:

  • that declares both dtype and one_of, or neither
  • of an undeclared subject, or of a dim with one_of
  • that refers to an undeclared dim or to a multi-dim
  • named like its subject's key column, or like a coordinate of its multi-dim
  • that categorises its subject and declares default_by

docs.title: partial
docs.text: partial is the set of dims along which the data one revision adds (a layer) overrides one value per label, a multi-dim among them. Layers states what a layer restates along any other dim. None, the default, declares a record with no layers. datarecord refuses a name in partial that the schema does not declare as a dim.

docs.title: meta
docs.text: meta is a dict of a framework's own data, such as network attributes or a coordinate reference system. datarecord stores it and never reads it.

docs.title: unit and description
docs.text: A Dimension, an AttributeSpec and a PropertySpec each take a unit and a description. datarecord stores both and reads neither, so it converts no unit. None means undeclared, and "" declares a quantity without a unit.

docs.title: Dtypes
docs.text:
A dtype is mathspec's DimensionDtype or ParameterDtype, written as its string. Each declaration maps to one DuckDB type:

Declares Declaration DuckDB type dim, attribute, property dtype: float DOUBLE dim, attribute, property dtype: int BIGINT attribute, property dtype: bool BOOLEAN dim, attribute, property dtype: str VARCHAR dim dtype: datetime TIMESTAMP (no time zone) dim one_of: [labels] ENUM of the labels multi-dim over: {...} STRUCT, a field per coordinate typed as its dim property one_of: <dim> that dim's type

An attribute takes no one_of, and no attribute or property is datetime. A property whose values are times refers to a datetime dim. The format fixes three more columns: attribute VARCHAR, breakpoint DOUBLE and value, typed as the attribute's dtype.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
A declared dim, coordinate, attribute or property name becomes a column, and datarecord refuses a name that cannot be one:

  • a name that is not ASCII letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, which is mathspec's rule for a name
  • a column datarecord writes, compared ignoring case: attribute, breakpoint, breakpoints, broadcast, layer_uuid, order_key, value and varies
  • a name that starts with _
  • two names that differ only in case, which DuckDB reads as one column

One spelling declared twice is one column and passes, as when a coordinate shares its dim's name. Labels are data, and these rules do not apply to them.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
schema.compatible_with(other) returns one reason for each way that layers written under other would not read under schema, and an empty list when they would. Store.commit checks a child's schema against its parent's this way and refuses an incompatible one before it writes any data.

Change Compatible add a dim, an attribute or a property yes add a dim to an attribute's dims yes add a dim to partial yes change a default, default_by, unit or description yes remove a dim, an attribute or a property no change a dtype, a one_of or an over no remove a dim from an attribute's dims no remove a dim from partial no

Moving a name between attributes and properties, or between subjects, removes it, so compatible_with reports it. An incompatible change needs the record rewritten under the new schema, such as a standalone directory written with ws.write.

docs.title: One schema per record
docs.text:
A record is read under the schema of its last layer. Each layer's file of its id, parent and files (its manifest) has the full schema the layer was written under. A root's schema is free, and a child's passes compatible_with against its parent's, so two sibling branches may declare one new name differently. A WorkingRecord reads and commits under its base's schema.

See also

  • The data model defines what each key declares.
  • Layers describes partial and what a layer restates.
  • Declare a schema shows the steps.
  • The Schema API lists every method.

docs.title: Selecting
docs.text: A selection is the Selection that select(record, **labels) returns: a record at the labels named. select reads the labels as xarray's sel does. One label squeezes its dim out of the selection, and a list, a slice or a partial date string keeps it.

docs.title: The call
docs.text:
from datarecord import select

view = select(record, snapshot=1)
view.labels

{'snapshot': 1}

select takes any RecordLike, a framework's own object included, and record.select(**labels) calls it on a Record. A Selection is itself a RecordLike, with three more members:

Member Value base the record selected from, never a Selection labels the keywords asked for, normalised: one label for a squeezed dim, else a list of labels schema the base's schema without the squeezed dims and what refers to them

labels has what you asked for, and the labels that a selection drops through references show only in view.dims. view.select(**labels) merges its keywords into labels, a later keyword replacing one of the same name, and selects base once.

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text:
A keyword is the name of one of three things:

  • A dim, such as snapshot=1 or bus=["north"].
  • A coordinate of a multi-dim that is no dim, such as from= of a corridor, which narrows the multi-dim's tuples.
  • A property by its plain name, which narrows its subject to the labels whose value, its default applied, is selected. A label whose value is NULL goes.

A coordinate or property keyword never squeezes, so labels has its value as a list. A tuple is selected through its coordinates, never by the multi-dim's own name.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
Value Selects The dim one label that label, as pandas' .loc matches it squeezed a partial date string, on a datetime axis every label in its span kept, even at one a list each label exactly, read as the dim's dtype kept, even at one slice(start, stop) the labels between, both ends included, None open kept, even at one

A date string is partial where it is coarser than the axis, so "2013-02" on a daily axis selects February and "2013-02-01" selects one label. In a list, a date string is one instant. A slice takes an axis of numbers or datetimes and compares its ends with the labels sorted, so snapshot=slice(1, None) gives [1, 2]. The labels a selection keeps are in axis order.

select raises ValueError at the call, naming the keyword, for:

  • a name that the schema declares as no dim, coordinate or property, or as a multi-dim
  • a property name that several subjects declare, or a coordinate name that several multi-dims declare
  • a label the axis lacks, or an empty list
  • a slice with a step, of an axis of text, with an end the axis cannot compare, or covering no label
  • a squeezed label that another keyword's selection drops
  • squeezing every dim of a record that declares attributes, because attribute data over no dim is no record
  • a squeeze that would change a default, as Squeezing describes

docs.title: Squeezing
docs.text:
To squeeze is to select one label of a dim, which drops the dim from the selection's schema. A list of one keeps the dim. Squeezing snapshot at 1 keeps the rows at 1 and the rows NULL on snapshot, settles them along snapshot alone, and drops the column:

Squeezing snapshot at one label The record's p_max_pu has rows for wind at snapshots 0, 1 and 2 and a row with entity and snapshot NULL. Squeezing snapshot at 1 drops the rows at snapshots 0 and 2, keeps the row at 1, settles the NULL row to snapshot 1, and drops the snapshot column: the selection contains wind 0.8 and entity NULL 1.0. record p_max_pu entity snapshot value wind 0 0.3 wind 1 0.8 wind 2 0.5 NULL NULL 1.0 selection snapshot squeezed entity value wind 0.8 NULL 1.0 squeeze keep snapshot 1, drop the column record read selection dropped by the selection

wind has the value it had at snapshot 1, and the NULL row stays NULL on entity.

Squeezing a dim d at a label l changes the schema and the rows:

  • d leaves the schema with its axis and its properties, and so does every property that refers to d.
  • A default_by keyed on a property that refers to d applies its entry for l as the default. A default_by keyed on a property of d applies the entry for the category that l has.
  • A multi-dim that draws on d loses that coordinate. One left with no coordinate is squeezed too.
  • An attribute over squeezed dims alone becomes one value over no dim.
  • partial and every Flags lose d.

record.select(ctype="Generator") squeezes ctype, so entity.ctype leaves the schema and the default of p_max_pu is 1.0, the Generator entry being absent. Where a default_by lists l and a kept label is NULL on the property, select refuses the squeeze. That label would take the default for l in the selection and not in the base. A list of one, such as ctype=["Load"], keeps the property and every default.

docs.title: What goes with a dropped label
docs.text:
A selection keeps every axis closed under reference, as removing a label does (layers):

  • A label whose property, its default applied, is a dropped label goes. A NULL is not a label and stays.
  • A tuple that contains a dropped label goes, and its other labels stay.
  • An attribute row that has a dropped label, in its column or in a field of a struct, goes. A row NULL there stays and applies to the kept labels.
  • This repeats until nothing more goes.
Dropping a bus drops the connections that contain it Selecting the bus north drops the bus south. The connection axis lists wind north, gas south, dc north and dc south, and the tuples gas south and dc south go with the dropped label. The selection keeps the bus north and the connections wind north and dc north. The entity axis keeps wind, gas and dc, because nothing flows back from a dropped tuple to the labels in it. axis bus bus north south axis connection entity bus wind north gas south dc north dc south axis bus bus north axis connection entity bus wind north dc north keep north drop the tuples that contain south entity keeps wind, gas and dc record read selection dropped by the selection

select(bus=["north"]) drops the bus south and the two connections that contain it.

Nothing flows the other way. A dim keeps a label that no kept label refers to, such as a carrier that no entity has. record.select(ctype="Generator") drops dc through entity.ctype and keeps the bus south.

docs.title: Laziness and layers
docs.text:
select reads the axes and properties it needs when you call it, and every attribute stays a plan on the base's connection. A selection needs neither the data each revision adds (its layers) nor partial. view.flags() returns the base's flags without the squeezed dims, which overstate the selection's rows.

A selection writes nothing, and WorkingRecord refuses one. Over a WorkingRecord, a narrowed axis keeps the labels it had at the call, and an attribute reads later edits at those labels.

docs.title: lift
docs.text:
To lift is to put the squeezed labels back on rows written over a selection, with Selection.lift. view.lift(attribute, rel) adds a column at its label for each squeezed dim of the attribute, and puts a squeezed coordinate back into its struct:

lift puts the squeezed label back Rows of p_max_pu over a selection that squeezed snapshot at 1 have the columns entity and value: wind 0.8 and NULL 1.0. lift adds the snapshot column at the label 1, so the rows read wind 1 0.8 and NULL 1 1.0. rows over the selection p_max_pu entity value wind 0.8 NULL 1.0 lifted rows p_max_pu entity snapshot value wind 1 0.8 NULL 1 1.0 lift add snapshot = 1 rows given lifted rows

The rows of p_max_pu over select(record, snapshot=1) come back with snapshot at 1.

lift reads only labels and the base's schema. It returns an attribute that the base declares over no squeezed dim unchanged, so lift("p_nom", rel) returns rel. The coordinates come back in the base's column order. A row NULL on the squeezed dim in the base was settled to the label, so it comes back at the label. lift raises KeyError when the base declares no such attribute.

See also

  • The record describes the members a selection shares with every record.
  • The data model defines the broadcast rule that a squeeze applies.
  • Select part of a record shows the steps.
  • The record API lists select and Selection.

docs.title: Workspace and store
docs.text:
This page describes Workspace, Store, Claim and Revision, in the order you use them. A workspace is the DuckDB database and the file access that its stores share, so records from several stores join. A store is one location, local or on S3, that contains the layers of a tree of revisions.

from datarecord import Workspace

ws = Workspace()  # ":memory:" by default
store = ws.store("/data/my-record")
root = store.commit(source, parent=None)
record = ws.write(source, "out/")

root is a revision of the store, and record is a standalone directory read back.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
Member Does Workspace(database=":memory:") opens the DuckDB database, in memory or in a file con returns the calling thread's cursor on the database store(uri) returns the workspace's one Store for the normalised location write(source, uri, *, meta=None) writes source as a standalone directory and returns it as a Record at(uri) reads the standalone directory at uri as a Record registered() returns the registered table unregister(name) drops a registration Workspace.process() returns the process's default workspace, created on first use close() closes the database and every thread's cursor

A location is a local path or an s3:// URI, and any other scheme raises ValueError. store("") raises, and a local path is resolved when you call store, write or at, so a later chdir does not change the location.

The record's data lies at the location, and the database contains only caches and staged edits. Deleting a workspace's database file loses at most the edits not yet committed. In a file-backed database, staged edits survive a crash and the manifest cache lasts across runs.

docs.title: A standalone directory
docs.text:
A standalone directory is one layer at its own URI, with a manifest that lists no parent. ws.write writes the data and then the manifest, under a fresh id, and refuses a URI where anything exists:

FileExistsError: /data/out/ already exists; a standalone record is written to a URI that does not exist yet

Locally, an empty directory counts as existing, and remotely any key under the URI does. A write that fails leaves its data files at the URI and no manifest, so a second write there raises until the files are deleted.

ws.at raises FileNotFoundError for a URI with no manifest.json, and ValueError for a manifest that lists a parent. store.layer(id) reads one layer of a store alone.

docs.title: The database
docs.text:
The tables that a workspace creates lie in DuckDB schemas of their own:

Schema Contains Created by main schemas, revisions and registered the workspace _fold.<id> the tables of one revision's fold the first cursor to fold <id> _staged.<id> a WorkingRecord's staging tables WorkingRecord(...) _scratch a call's intermediate tables the call, which drops them <name> the views of a registration record.register(name)

<id> is the 32-digit hex of the revision's or layer's UUID. revisions and schemas cache each manifest whole, and gain rows only, so the cache can be incomplete and never stale.

The workspace keeps the _fold schemas of the layers a Record folds until record.close(), and a WorkingRecord's _staged schema until it closes. It keeps the schemas of a registered record until unregister. The workspace drops a schema once no open record or registration reads it. A closed record raises ValueError on every read, and a Record collected unclosed leaves its schemas to the workspace until the workspace closes.

docs.title: Files, local and remote
docs.text:
Manifests, claims, listing layers/ and deleting a pending layer go through the workspace's Files, which datarecord picks by the URI's scheme. DuckDB reads and writes the parquet.

class Files(Protocol):
    def read_text(self, uri: str) -> str | None: ...
    def create(self, uri: str, text: str) -> None: ...
    def list(self, prefix: str) -> list[str]: ...
    def exists(self, uri: str) -> bool: ...
    def delete(self, prefix: str) -> None: ...

create writes only where nothing is, and raises PreconditionFailedError otherwise. Locally it writes under a temporary name and hard-links the file into place, so a read finds a whole file or none.

An s3:// URI needs the optional extra datarecord[remote], which installs the boto3 package. Remotely, create is a put_object with IfNoneMatch="*", which the server must honour, as AWS S3 does and SeaweedFS does from version 4.18 on. Credentials and the endpoint come from the AWS environment and config files. Where AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is set, DuckDB's S3 secret takes its endpoint with path-style URLs, for a self-hosted server.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
ws.con returns the calling thread's cursor, so every thread can share one workspace, one store and one Record. Tables, registered views and fold results are shared between cursors. A DuckDBPyRelation and a WorkingRecord belong to the thread that built them. A write or an edit refuses a relation from another thread or connection:

ValueError: this relation was built on another connection or thread; build it on `record.con` in this thread, or hand over a pandas, polars or arrow frame to land

When two threads fold one revision at once, both fold and datarecord keeps one of the two tables, so each reads the same answer.

See also

Store a record shows a store, a directory, S3 and threads in use.

docs.title: Store
docs.text:
Member Does uri the absolute location claim(*, parent, meta=None) hands out a new layer id under parent and returns a Claim commit(source, *, parent, meta=None) claims and commits in one call, and returns the Revision commit(w, *, meta=None) writes a WorkingRecord's edits as a child of the revision it was built over revision(id) returns one revision, and raises KeyError for an id with no manifest revisions(*, meta=None) returns every revision, unordered, or those whose meta has every pair given claims() returns the pending layers, oldest first cleanup(*, ids=None, older_than=None) deletes pending layers and returns their ids layer(id) reads one layer alone as a Record

parent is a required keyword, so a new root is parent=None. revisions(meta={"run": 1}) matches a value of the same type only, so 1 matches neither 1.0 nor True.

docs.title: The steps of a commit
docs.text:
A write to a store runs in three steps:

Step File Write Contains claim claim.json create-only id, parent, meta, when it was taken data dims/, attributes/ unconditional the layer's parquet commit manifest.json create-only the manifest

A layer with a claim and no manifest is pending, and no read, listing or ancestry() finds it. A commit that fails leaves its layer pending with the files it wrote, and a retried commit writes them again.

Before it writes data, a commit checks three things and refuses the layer otherwise:

  • The layer's schema passes compatible_with against the parent's manifest's schema.
  • Its meta has every key of the claim's meta with the same value, and may add keys.
  • Its parent is a revision of this store.

store.commit(w) takes w's base as the parent and raises TypeError for a parent passed beside it. Over a base that is no revision of this store, such as a standalone directory, it refuses w and names ws.write(w, uri), which writes w whole.

docs.title: Claim
docs.text:
A Claim is a revision id that a store reserves before the layer is written. It has id, store, parent, meta and created, and claim.commit(source, *, meta=None) writes the layer and returns the Revision.

A claim serialises as its store's location and its id, and pickles the same way. A job in another process can then commit it, days later if need be. A claim has one committer at a time. A commit raises ValueError once a cleanup deleted its claim.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
Only cleanup deletes, and only a pending layer:

store.cleanup(ids=[claim.id])
store.cleanup(older_than=timedelta(days=14))

cleanup takes exactly one of ids and older_than, and raises ValueError before it deletes anything if an id is not pending. It checks each layer for a manifest again right before deleting it, without a lock. A cleanup that races a commit can still delete a layer that is committing, so pass ids or an age that match no running job.

docs.title: Concurrent writers
docs.text: Each writer claims a fresh id and writes into its own layer directory, so two writers never write the same file. Two writers that widen one parent's schema at once both commit, each child under its own schema. materialise() writes the one kind of file that is not create-only, and two writers that materialise one revision write the same content.

docs.title: Revision
docs.text:
A Revision is the id of one layer in a store. The layers page lists its members.

A revision serialises as its id and its store's location, and pickles the same way:

payload = rev.model_dump_json()  # {"id": "4731e41b-…", "store": "/data/my-record"}
rev = Revision.model_validate_json(payload)  # in another process

The second process loads the revision onto Workspace.process() and reads its manifest and each parent's, so rev.ancestry() returns there too.

rev.record builds the record once and returns the same one until you close it, then builds another.

See also

The storage page argues for the manifest written last and for writers that share no file. The API reference lists every signature.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: This page describes the Tool protocol, then the rules of the PyPSA tool in the order the tool reads a record and then writes one. A tool is a module under datarecord.tools that translates between a record and one modelling framework.

docs.title: The Tool protocol
docs.text:
class Tool(Protocol):
    name: str
    schema: Schema

    def requires(self, record: RecordLike) -> Requirements: ...
    def verify(self, record: RecordLike) -> Requirements: ...
    def build(self, record: RecordLike) -> Any: ...
    def to_datarecord(
        self,
        model: Any,
        con: DuckDBPyConnection,
        *,
        results_only: bool = False,
        base: RecordLike | None = None,
    ) -> RecordLike: ...
Member Does name is the framework's name, which error messages quote schema is the map from the tool's attribute names to the record's (below) requires returns what the tool needs from this record: dims, categories and attributes verify returns what the record fails to supply, falsy when the tool can build it build returns the framework's own object, built from any RecordLike to_datarecord presents a framework object as a RecordLike whose relations are planned on con

Each tool's module defines the tool as a module-level object, such as PyPSA, and nothing outside datarecord.tools imports a tool. build reads record.con for its queries, so it builds from a standalone directory as it does from a revision. build raises UnsupportedRecordError for a record that verify finds unusable.

to_datarecord plans its relations on the connection it receives, which is ws.con of the workspace that writes them. Its result goes straight to store.commit or ws.write. base is the record the layer is committed over as a child, and the record the model was built from. With results_only=True it presents only what a solve produced, as a layer over base. It raises ValueError where results_only comes without base.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirements is what requires and verify return, with one set per kind of fault.

Field Contains dims dims the tool needs and the schema does not declare categories categories the framework has no counterpart for attributes (category, attribute) pairs with no value, named in the record's words unsupported_keys (key, dim) pairs of a partial the framework cannot take unsupported_dims dims the record declares that the framework's model has no place for unsupported_values (category, attribute) pairs stored as a curve, or varying along a dim the framework holds the attribute without names labels that two of the framework's categories share ignored (category, attribute) pairs that the record stores and the category does not take

A Requirements is truthy when any field but ignored has an entry. a | b returns a Requirements with the union of each field. describe() returns a one-line summary, which UnsupportedRecordError quotes.

docs.title: The tool's schema
docs.text:
A tool's Schema lists, per category, the tool attributes that are renamed or computed, each an Attr that lists its source attributes. An attribute with no entry keeps its name, so an empty Schema maps every name to itself. Attr.resolve settles each source attribute before it renames or computes, so a computed attribute combines one row per point of each source.

See also

Present a framework object as a record shows a tool author's to_datarecord.

docs.title: The PyPSA tool
docs.text:
from datarecord.tools.pypsa import PyPSA, PyPSACollection

The PyPSA tool needs the optional extra datarecord[pypsa]. PyPSA builds and writes a pypsa.Network, and PyPSACollection a pypsa.NetworkCollection. Their schema is empty, because the record's names are PyPSA's.

docs.title: The schema
docs.text:
to_datarecord writes every network under one schema, declared from PyPSA's component registry:

Dim Is entity a component of any type but Shape and those with a dim of their own ctype a dim with one_of: the component types bus, carrier, sub_network a bus, a carrier, a SubNetwork as PyPSA numbers it line_type, transformer_type a standard type connection a multi-dim over (entity, bus): one port of a component role a dim with one_of: input, output and attached snapshot a timestamp, or a multi-dim over (period, timestep) if multi-period timestep, period, scenario a timestep, an investment period by its year, a scenario Subject Properties entity ctype, carrier, sign, type bus carrier, type, x, y, unit, location carrier color, nice_name sub_network carrier line_type, transformer_type every registry input of the type connection role

partial is {"entity", "bus", "scenario", "connection"}. to_datarecord writes no axis of ctype or role, since a dim with one_of lists its labels. Every other registry input is an attribute, p_nom among them. Every component attribute is over scenario, except those PyPSA keeps the same in every scenario. These are active, build_year, committable, lifetime, weight, *_nom_extendable, *_nom_mod and the results *_nom_opt.

docs.title: verify
docs.text:
verify takes a record or a selection, and reports in a Requirements:

Field Entries dims snapshot, period or scenario, where the schema lacks it and no selection squeezes it unsupported_keys snapshot, where it is in partial unsupported_dims each dim of the record's own (a collection) categories each ctype that PyPSA's registry lacks attributes each required attribute with no row, property or declared default, a port's bus among them unsupported_values each attribute stored as a curve, or varying along a dim PyPSA holds it without ignored each attribute a type has a value for and does not take

When verify finds an unsupported key or dim, it reports nothing else. It raises ValueError for a selection that build refuses.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: build builds each type's static frame from its entities, their properties and the rows of attributes over entity alone. A default that differs per type, such as sign or p_set, is a default_by on entity.ctype. A row with entity NULL applies to each member of the type build builds.

docs.title: Buses and carriers
docs.text:
A bus is a label of bus, and a carrier is a label of carrier:

PyPSA Record Bus.type, carrier, x, y, unit, location properties of bus Bus.v_nom, v_mag_pu_min, v_mag_pu_max, v_mag_pu_set attributes over bus Bus.marginal_price, v_mag_pu, v_ang result attributes over bus Bus.p, q, control, generator, sub_network not written Line.v_nom, ShuntImpedance.v_nom not written SubNetwork.obj not written Carrier.color, nice_name properties of carrier Carrier.co2_emissions, max_growth, max_relative_growth attributes over carrier a component's carrier entity.carrier, which refers to carrier a custom column see custom columns

bus.x is a bus's x position, and x a line's reactance. bus.carrier defaults to AC.

docs.title: Standard types
docs.text: A line type is a label of line_type, and a transformer type a label of transformer_type. Every registry column of a type is a property of its dim, so transformer_type.s_nom is apart from a transformer's attribute s_nom. entity.type is text that refers to no dim. to_datarecord writes only the types that PyPSA's library lacks, and build adds them to the new network's library. A library type has the library's values in the built network.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Each port of a component is a connection tuple (entity, bus), and a per-port input or result is an attribute over connection. build turns the tuples of a component back into PyPSA's numbered columns:

build places a component's ports by connection order The record contains the connection tuples link1 north, with role input, and link1 south, with role output, and efficiency 0.9 on link1 south. build writes n.links with bus0 north, bus1 south and efficiency 0.9. record dims/connection connection role (link1, north) input (link1, south) output attributes/efficiency connection value (link1, south) 0.9 n.links name bus0 bus1 efficiency link1 north south 0.9 build the input first, then connection order

bus0 is the connection with role input, and the other ports follow in axis order. The efficiency row at the second port is PyPSA's efficiency, and at a third port it is efficiency2. A Process's rate0, rate1, … are the one attribute rate. rate declares no default, and a port with no row keeps PyPSA's default for that port. delay and cyclic_delay are over connection. A one-port component's connection has the role attached.

docs.title: Results on connections
docs.text: p0, p1, … of a Line, Transformer, Link or Process are the attribute p over connection. So is the one-port p of a Generator, Load, Store, StorageUnit or ShuntImpedance. Each row has PyPSA's sign for its port, and q0, q1 and q are q. A Link's and a Process's own p is p_internal over entity.

docs.title: Custom columns
docs.text:
A custom column is a static column that PyPSA's registry lacks, placed on its type's dim:

Custom column Placed as a text column, such as Bus.country a property, bus.country a column of a standard type a property a column that types of two dims have, or that the registry declares over other dims a property any other column, such as Bus.nom_max_onwind_2050 an attribute over the dim

A custom property takes its dtype from its values, and has no default. A text property named like a dim refers to that dim. meta["custom_columns"] lists each entity type's custom columns. to_datarecord raises ValueError for a custom property that two types of one dim have with two dtypes. It also raises for a value of a referring property that names no label. It raises for a custom column on a Shape, or named shape_…, snapshot, timestep, period, scenario, entity or connection.

docs.title: A value its type does not take
docs.text: A row with entity NULL applies to every entity, so set("p_max_pu", 0.9) applies to a load too. build gives each type only its registry inputs and results, its custom columns, and the names that no type takes. verify lists each left-out (type, attribute) in ignored. build also leaves out an entity property that a type does not take, and verify does not list it.

docs.title: Snapshots and weightings
docs.text:
A single-period snapshot is a datetime dim. A multi-period snapshot is a multi-dim over (period, timestep), where timestep has each timestep once. build rebuilds PyPSA's index from the tuples in axis order. set takes a multi-period snapshot by period and timestep together, and refuses one alone.

Attribute Over scenario_weight scenario snapshot_weighting_objective, snapshot_weighting_stores, snapshot_weighting_generators snapshot period_weighting_objective, period_weighting_years period

A label that no weighting row applies to keeps PyPSA's default, which for a scenario is an equal share.

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
A shape is the property shape_{type} of the label idx it outlines, as well-known text (WKT) of dtype str. A Bus shape is a property of bus, and an entity type's of entity. Any other component, such as country, is a dim of that name, outside partial, with the shapes' idx as labels. Such a dim is no dim of the record's own. So Germany's offshore waters are country.shape_offshore at label DE.

to_datarecord raises ValueError for a shape without a component, an idx or a type, and for two shapes with one (component, idx, type). It also raises for an idx that names no label its type writes, and for a component that names a dim of the PyPSA schema. meta["crs"] is the network's coordinate reference system, such as EPSG:3035. to_datarecord does not write PyPSA's srid. build sets the CRS before it adds a component, and uses EPSG:4326 where meta has no crs. build names each shape "{component} {idx} {type}", such as "Bus DE onshore".

docs.title: Selecting before a build
docs.text:
build and verify take a selection as they take a record:

Selected One label A list, a slice or a partial date period a single-period network, without investment_period a multi-period network scenario a deterministic network a stochastic network, weights renormalised to 1 a dim of the record's own the member at that label a PyPSACollection build another dim, such as snapshot or bus refused the network at those labels

build then drops each period left without snapshots, and each entity attached to a dropped bus. Over fewer periods than the record has, it drops each entity active in none, where build_year <= period < build_year + lifetime. An entity without a row of build_year or lifetime takes the declared default, else 0 or infinity. build also drops each GlobalConstraint whose investment_period names a dropped period, and keeps one with investment_period NULL. A kept scenario that no scenario_weight row applies to takes its equal share of the record's scenarios before the renormalisation. build raises ValueError for a selection with no snapshot, and for kept scenarios whose weights sum to 0. It raises for an attribute whose rows name several labels of a dim PyPSA holds it without, such as marginal_cost over period. Over fewer periods, it raises where build_year, lifetime or investment_period varies along a dim the selection keeps.

docs.title: Writing results
docs.text:
to_datarecord(n, con) writes the whole network, its frames in PyPSA's order. It adds each carrier that n.carriers lacks, writes PyPSA's "" carrier as NULL, and writes a value shared by every scenario with scenario NULL. It leaves out a static value at its default, so an unsolved network has no result. It writes each input at a port, at its default too, and each custom column placed as an attribute. It raises UnsupportedRecordError for two types with one name, and ValueError for a property that differs between scenarios.

to_datarecord(n, con, base=record) writes only what changed from base:

Value Written where a static value it differs from base's resolved value, or from the default where base has none a series whole, where it differs from base's at one snapshot or more an axis whole, always

A value with scenario NULL is left out only where base resolves the same value at each scenario. An input at a port or a custom column placed as an attribute is written wherever base has no value for it. A value set back to its default over a base with another is written. Values compare exactly, and NULL equals NULL. to_datarecord raises ValueError where base is a selection, has a dim of its own, or has other investment periods than the network.

to_datarecord(n, con, results_only=True, base=record) presents only the solve's results:

results = PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, ws.con, results_only=True, base=inputs.record)
solved = store.commit(results, parent=inputs)
  • The layer has the results and the intermediate results they need, at their defaults too. It has no input, shape or standard type.
  • A result of base that the solve does not write again is NULL, at the scenarios, buses, entities and connections the network has.
  • A series is written at the network's snapshots, and base's values stand at the others.
  • Over a multi-period base, a result such as p_nom_opt is written for the entities active in the network's periods.
  • Over a selection, lift puts each row back at the squeezed labels.
  • The layer restates the sub_network axis with the solve's SubNetworks, empty where the solve has none. It writes no such axis where neither the solve nor base has one.
  • Over a network with fewer buses or entities than base, the layer leaves the sub_network axis to base. It also leaves to base the results that name a SubNetwork, such as slack_bus and a line's sub_network.

With results_only=True, to_datarecord raises ValueError for:

  • a missing base.
  • a network with a snapshot, bus or entity that base lacks.
  • a deterministic network over a base with scenarios, rather than over the selection at one scenario.
  • a result over no scenario from fewer scenarios than the record has.
  • a multi-period network over a single-period base, or a single-period one over a multi-period base that squeezes no period.
  • a network over a record with a dim of its own, rather than over the selection at one label.

docs.title: A collection
docs.text:
PyPSACollection writes and builds a pypsa.NetworkCollection, each member through PyPSA. Its dim is the name of the collection's one index level, either period or a dim of the record's own. A record has at most one dim of its own. to_datarecord checks every member before it returns, and raises ValueError for:

  • base without results_only=True.
  • an index of more than one level, or one named for a dim of the PyPSA schema but period.
  • an index named for a dim that the members' shapes make.
  • a base with another dim of its own.
  • members that differ where they must agree.
  • a member that orders shared labels otherwise than the members before it.

Two floats agree within numpy.isclose's default tolerance, and other values agree where equal. The record's meta and crs are the first member's. verify checks each member as PyPSA.verify checks a selection, and reports what any member lacks. build raises ValueError for a single-period record without a dim of its own. verify reports each dim of its own of a record with several in unsupported_dims, and build raises UnsupportedRecordError for it.

docs.title: Over period
docs.text: to_datarecord writes a myopic solve as one multi-period network with every member's period. Each member is deterministic and has its own period alone. Two members that hold an entity active and give it different static values are refused. An asset that a later member lacks is retired, its lifetime ending at the first period without it. An asset held again after a gap is refused. to_datarecord numbers the SubNetworks once for the whole network. build gives member p as PyPSA.build(record.select(period=[p])).

docs.title: Over a dim of its own
docs.text:
to_datarecord adds the dim to the schema and to partial. An attribute whose values agree across the members is written once, as declared, and one whose values differ varies over the dim. A later layer whose values differ widens the attribute's dims by the dim. Members must have the same snapshots, components, schema and custom columns. Their axes are one union in the first member's order, and a label's properties agree across them. build gives member label as PyPSA.build(record.select(dim=label)). Results of a collection of fewer labels than base has are at each member's label, even where the members agree. They leave the other labels, the dim's axis and the SubNetworks to base. to_datarecord raises ValueError for a member's label that base's axis of the dim lacks.

See also

Use the PyPSA tool shows a build, a solve, a selection, a change-only export and a collection. The API reference lists every signature.

docs.title: WorkingRecord
docs.text:
WorkingRecord(base: RecordLike)

Bases: Record

A Record whose last source is a staging area, plus the edit surface.

A Record in the type as well as in the fold: what it reads is the data with its pending edits applied, and it reads it by being one layer deeper than its base rather than by overlaying anything of its own. Every read member is inherited unchanged, so an edit reads back through the same code path a committed layer would.

Staged rows live in connection-scoped DuckDB tables, the only place a staged row exists: the reads fold them rather than holding a copy, so what is staged is asked of the reads themselves.

The source list is fixed at construction and never changes; a set changes what the last source's tables hold, not which sources there are. That is what lets the inherited members stay correct - they cache a key set only where the fold is stable, which a staged source makes it not.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

On a read, an edit or edits once the record is closed, and on an edit or edits once a WorkingRecord it is staged over is.

Notes
  • WorkingRecord
  • staging
  • reading with pending edits

Where the cursor holds an open transaction, whose staging tables no other cursor could see to drop.

def __init__(self, base: RecordLike) -> None:
    """Stage edits over `base`, which must be a `Record`.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        For any other `RecordLike`, naming `ws.write(source, uri)`, which
        gives one.
    duckdb.TransactionException
        Where the cursor holds an open transaction, whose staging tables no
        other cursor could see to drop.

    Notes
    -----
    - [WorkingRecord](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/)
    """
    if not isinstance(base, Record):
        msg = (
            f"a `WorkingRecord` folds its staged rows over a `Record`'s layers, "
            f"and a {type(base).__name__} has none: write it first, "
            f"`WorkingRecord(ws.write(source, uri))`"
        )
        raise TypeError(msg)
    refuse_open_transaction(
        base.con,
        "WorkingRecord",
        "https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#transactions-and-staging",
    )
    # `object.__setattr__` throughout: the base is a frozen dataclass, and
    # these are set before `super().__init__` because the `StagedSource`
    # below reads them off `self`.
    object.__setattr__(self, "_layer_id", uuid4())
    object.__setattr__(self, "_staged", {})
    object.__setattr__(self, "_touched", set())
    object.__setattr__(self, "_dirty", set())
    if not isinstance(base, WorkingRecord):
        base = _Base(base.revision_id, base.sources, base.workspace)
    object.__setattr__(self, "_base", base)
    object.__setattr__(self, "_staging_schema", nested(STAGED, self._layer_id))
    base.con.execute(f"CREATE SCHEMA {self._staging_schema}")
    super().__init__(
        base.revision_id,
        [*base.sources, StagedSource(self, self._layer_id)],
        base.workspace,
    )
    if isinstance(base, _Base):
        object.__setattr__(base, "_release", self._release)
        object.__setattr__(base, "_holder", self._holder)
    for kind, attribute in self._kinds():
        name = self._table(kind, attribute)
        self._shape(kind, attribute).create(name)
        self._staged[kind, attribute] = name
        self._fill(kind, attribute)
    shape = self._table(_OWNERS)
    empty = empty_relation(self.con, attribute=sqltypes.VARCHAR)
    owner_keys(empty, self.schema, self._layer_id, ()).create(shape)
    for attribute in self.schema.attributes:
        name = self._table(_OWNERS, attribute)
        self.con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {name} AS FROM {shape}")
        self._staged[_OWNERS, attribute] = name
    self.con.execute(f"DROP TABLE {shape}")
    self._frozen_owners  # noqa: B018 - built outside any edit's transaction

docs.title: set
docs.text:
set(attribute: str, value: Any, **coords: Any) -> None

Stage values of one attribute.

Every coordinate is a keyword - entity=, snapshot=, a multi-dim's coordinate such as bus= or a corridor's from= - since which exist is declared rather than fixed. A keyword holds one label, fixing that coordinate, or a list of labels the value is staged at each of. A coordinate no keyword names is NULL, which by the broadcast rule is every label of it. The call replaces every row of attribute staged earlier that its own rows cover.

value takes five forms:

  • a scalar, staged at every combination of the listed labels;
  • a sequence, aligned positionally to the one list keyword;
  • a mapping or a one-dimensional labelled series, keyed by labels of the series' index.name where that names a coordinate, else of the one coordinate no keyword names;
  • a long frame supplying its own keys, which keywords may complete with single labels.

An attribute's values are long rows, whatever its dims. A property - a category included - patches one column of existing axis rows: a mapping or series from label to value, a dim= keyword naming the labels, or a scalar for every label the axis has. A multi-dim's property takes a scalar, its coordinates as keywords selecting the tuples, none selecting every tuple. A coordinate is part of the key, which add and remove change, and is refused here.

A property is named subject.name - set("entity.carrier", ...) - and a plain name is an attribute.

A keyword naming no coordinate of attribute is a property of a dim it reaches - ctype="Generator", or a list of values - and selects the labels of that dim matching it on the record as staged, the keywords combining as an intersection; set writes one row per label, and stores nothing of the filter, so a label added later is not reached. A property of a multi-dim attribute is over - role="output" - selects its tuples the same way, narrowed by any keyword naming one of its coordinates. On a multi-dim's property, the keywords select its tuples as on an attribute over it: set("connection.note", v, role="output") patches the output connections, and ctype="Link" the connections of links.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

On an undeclared attribute or keyword, a label that its dim's axis, as staged, does not hold, a tuple that its multi-dim, as staged, does not hold, a property's label no layer wrote, or a value of a property that refers to a dim and is no label of it.

ValueError

On a coordinate named as subject.name, a keyword the attribute does not vary over, a sequence with no single list keyword to align to, keys whose coordinate is ambiguous, a label its dim does not list, a property keyword whose dim the attribute does not reach through exactly one coordinate, or that is given beside that coordinate's own keyword, a frame column the schema does not declare for attribute, or a frame column or label whose type does not fit its dtype, timestamps with a time zone among them.

Notes
  • the shape of an edit
  • set
  • validation

@_atomic
def set(
    self,
    attribute: str,
    value: Any,
    **coords: Any,
) -> None:
    """Stage values of one attribute.

    Every coordinate is a keyword - `entity=`, `snapshot=`, a multi-dim's
    coordinate such as `bus=` or a corridor's `from=` - since which exist is declared
    rather than fixed. A keyword holds one label, fixing that coordinate, or
    a list of labels the value is staged at each of. A coordinate no keyword
    names is NULL, which by the broadcast rule is every label of it. The
    call replaces every row of `attribute` staged earlier that its own
    rows cover.

    `value` takes five forms:

    - a scalar, staged at every combination of the listed labels;
    - a sequence, aligned positionally to the one list keyword;
    - a mapping or a one-dimensional labelled series, keyed by labels of
      the series' `index.name` where that names a coordinate, else of the
      one coordinate no keyword names;
    - a long frame supplying its own keys, which keywords may complete with
      single labels.

    An attribute's values are long rows, whatever its `dims`. A property -
    a category included - patches one column of existing axis rows: a
    mapping or series from label to value, a `dim=` keyword naming the
    labels, or a scalar for every label the axis has. A multi-dim's
    property takes a scalar, its coordinates as keywords selecting the
    tuples, none selecting every tuple. A coordinate is part of the key,
    which `add` and `remove` change, and is refused here.

    A property is named `subject.name` - `set("entity.carrier", ...)` -
    and a plain name is an attribute.

    A keyword naming no coordinate of `attribute` is a property of a dim it
    reaches - `ctype="Generator"`, or a list of values - and selects
    the labels of that dim matching it on the record as staged, the
    keywords combining as an intersection; `set` writes one row per label,
    and stores nothing of the filter, so a label added later is not reached.
    A property of a multi-dim `attribute` is over - `role="output"` -
    selects its tuples the same way, narrowed by any keyword naming one of
    its coordinates. On a multi-dim's property, the keywords select its
    tuples as on an attribute over it: `set("connection.note", v,
    role="output")` patches the output connections, and `ctype="Link"`
    the connections of links.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        On an undeclared attribute or keyword, a label that its dim's
        axis, as staged, does not hold, a tuple that its multi-dim, as
        staged, does not hold, a property's label no layer wrote, or a
        value of a property that refers to a dim and is no
        label of it.
    ValueError
        On a coordinate named as `subject.name`, a keyword the attribute
        does not vary over, a sequence with no single list keyword to align to,
        keys whose coordinate is ambiguous, a label its dim does not
        list, a property keyword whose dim the attribute does not reach
        through exactly one coordinate, or that is given beside that
        coordinate's own keyword, a frame column the schema does not
        declare for `attribute`, or a frame column or label whose type
        does not fit its dtype, timestamps with a time zone among them.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the shape of an edit](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#the-shape-of-an-edit)
    - [set](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#set)
    - [validation](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#validation)
    """
    keyed = isinstance(value, Mapping) or _series_index(value) is not None
    if isinstance(self.schema.resolve(attribute), tuple):
        self._set_dotted(attribute, value, coords)
        return
    coords, tuples = self._select(attribute, coords)
    listed = {c: list(v) for c, v in coords.items() if _is_labels(v)}

    if is_frame(value) and not keyed:
        if listed or tuples:
            msg = (
                f"`set({attribute!r}, <frame>)` supplies its own keys, so "
                f"keywords {sorted(listed)} may give one label each, not a "
                f"list, and none may select the tuples of {sorted(tuples)}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        call = f"`set({attribute!r}, <frame>)`"
        rel = as_relation(value, self.con)
        multi_dims = self.schema.multi_dims_of(attribute)
        self.schema.check_multi_dim_columns(multi_dims, rel, carrier=call)
        self.schema.refuse_partial_tuples(multi_dims, rel, carrier=call)
        self._validate_input(attribute, coords)
        table = self._ensure(_ATTRIBUTES, attribute)
        known = [
            *self._staged_coordinates(attribute),
            *_flat_coordinates(self.schema, attribute),
            "value",
        ]
        extra = sorted(set(rel.columns) - set(known))
        if extra:
            msg = (
                f"{call} was given columns {extra} the schema does not "
                f"declare for {attribute!r}; it takes {sorted(set(known))}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        rel = self.schema.require_takes(rel, call, attribute=attribute)
        self._insert_long(rel, table, attribute, set(rel.columns), coords)
        return

    self._validate_input(attribute, coords)

    if keyed:
        selected = [c for m in tuples for c in self.schema.over(m)]
        key = self._key_coordinate(attribute, value, [*coords, *selected])
        keys, values = normalise_value(value)
        dim = _flat_coordinates(self.schema, attribute)[key]
        self._require_typed(
            dim, cast("list[Any]", keys), f"`set({attribute!r}, ...)`"
        )
        column: dict[str, Sequence[Any]] = {key: cast("list[Any]", keys)}
    elif _is_labels(value):
        if len(listed) != 1:
            msg = (
                f"`set({attribute!r}, <sequence>)` aligns to exactly one list "
                f"keyword, and was given {sorted(listed) or 'none'}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        ((key, labels),) = listed.items()
        del listed[key]
        _, values = normalise_value(value, labels)
        column = {key: labels}
    else:
        values = [value]
        column = {}
    rel = self._columns_relation(
        {**column, "value": values},
        {
            **{c: self._coordinate_type(attribute, c) for c in column},
            "value": None,
        },
    )
    for c, labels in listed.items():
        rel = rel.cross(
            self._columns_relation(
                {c: labels}, {c: self._coordinate_type(attribute, c)}
            )
        )
    for chosen in tuples.values():
        rel = rel.cross(chosen)
    fixed = {c: v for c, v in coords.items() if not _is_labels(v)}
    self._insert_long(
        rel,
        self._ensure(_ATTRIBUTES, attribute),
        attribute,
        set(rel.columns),
        fixed,
    )

add(
    dim: str,
    labels: Sequence[Any]
    | Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]
    | DuckDBPyRelation,
    **columns: Any,
) -> None

Stage labels of dim, each as one whole row of its axis file.

columns are dim's properties, each a scalar for every label or a sequence aligned to labels. A column no keyword names is NULL on these rows: add restates a label's row whole, replacing any this record staged for it. A label keeps its place in the axis, a label of the base removed here takes its base place back, and a new one is appended.

A multi-dim's labels are tuples, given as a frame holding the struct column named for the multi-dim, as dims[dim] reads it, or one with a column per coordinate instead, or as a list of mappings from coordinate to label. A frame may carry property columns too and takes a scalar keyword only.

Not a sequence of set calls: a label exists by virtue of its axis row, so adding one with no columns at all is an edit. An attribute's value, whatever its dims, goes through set.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If the schema declares no dim, on a value of a property that refers to a dim and is no label of it, or on a tuple naming a label its coordinate's axis, as staged, does not hold.

TypeError

On a frame for a dim that is no multi-dim, or a value that is no frame DuckDB rescans.

ValueError

On a dim with one_of, whose axis is the schema's, an attribute, a column the axis file has no place for, a sequence of the wrong length, a property value its dim does not list, a label whose type does not fit the dtype of dim, a tuple missing a coordinate or naming NULL in one, or a frame carrying both the struct column and a coordinate column.

@_atomic
def add(
    self,
    dim: str,
    labels: Sequence[Any] | Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | DuckDBPyRelation,
    **columns: Any,
) -> None:
    """Stage labels of `dim`, each as one whole row of its axis file.

    `columns` are `dim`'s properties, each a scalar for every label or a
    sequence aligned to `labels`. A column no keyword names is NULL on
    these rows: `add` restates a label's row whole, replacing any this
    record staged for it. A label keeps its place in the axis, a label of
    the base removed here takes its base place back, and a new one is
    appended.

    A multi-dim's labels are tuples, given as a frame holding the struct
    column named for the multi-dim, as `dims[dim]` reads it, or one with a
    column per coordinate instead, or as a list of mappings from
    coordinate to label. A frame may carry property columns too and takes
    a scalar keyword only.

    Not a sequence of `set` calls: a label exists by virtue of its axis row,
    so adding one with no columns at all is an edit. An attribute's value,
    whatever its `dims`, goes through `set`.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the schema declares no `dim`, on a value of a property
        that refers to a dim and is no label of it, or on a tuple naming
        a label its coordinate's axis, as staged, does not hold.
    TypeError
        On a frame for a dim that is no multi-dim, or a value that is no
        frame DuckDB rescans.
    ValueError
        On a dim with `one_of`, whose axis is the schema's, an
        attribute, a column the axis file has no place for, a sequence of
        the wrong length, a property value its dim does not list, a label
        whose type does not fit the dtype of `dim`, a tuple missing a
        coordinate or naming NULL in one, or a frame carrying both the
        struct column and a coordinate column.

    Notes
    -----
    - [add / remove](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#add-and-remove)
    - [where a value lives](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#where-a-value-lives)
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#multi-dims)
    """
    if dim not in self.schema.dimensions:
        msg = f"the schema declares no dim {dim!r}"
        raise KeyError(msg)
    call = f"add({dim!r}, ...)"
    self._refuse_one_of(dim, f"`{call}`")
    if dim in self.schema.multi_dims:
        self._add_tuples(dim, labels, columns)
        return
    kind = f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{dim}"
    names = _plain_labels(dim, labels, f"`{call}`")
    self._reject_undeclared(f"`{call}`", _axis_columns(self.schema, dim), columns)
    self._require_typed(dim, names, f"`{call}`")
    data: dict[str, list[Any]] = {dim: names}
    for c, given in columns.items():
        data[c] = list(given) if _is_labels(given) else [given] * len(names)
        if len(data[c]) != len(names):
            msg = (
                f"`{call}` has {len(data[c])} {c!r} values for {len(names)} labels"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
    self.schema.require_one_of(dim, data, f"`{call}`")
    self._require_live(dim, data, f"`{call}`")
    rel = self._columns_relation(data, {c: self._column_type(c, dim) for c in data})
    table = self._ensure(kind)
    self._insert_snapshot(
        self._positioned(rel, table, kind, dim), table, {}, key=(dim,)
    )

@_atomic
def remove(
    self,
    dim: str,
    labels: Sequence[Any] | Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | DuckDBPyRelation,
) -> None:
    """Stage `dim`'s axis without `labels`.

    Need not enumerate what it deletes: the fold drops every value keyed
    by a removed label where `dim` is `partial`. No labels stage nothing.

    And every multi-dim with a coordinate over `dim` without the tuples
    naming one of `labels`, read from the record as it currently resolves:
    a multi-dim attribute's value goes with its tuple.

    A multi-dim's labels are tuples, given as `add` takes them.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        As `add` does.
    ValueError
        On a dim with `one_of`, whose axis is the schema's, a label whose
        type does not fit the dtype of `dim`, a tuple given as `add`
        refuses it, or while a property that refers to `dim` stores one of
        `labels` in the record as staged.

    Notes
    -----
    - [add / remove](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#add-and-remove)
    - [deletion](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/layers/#removing-labels)
    """
    call = f"`remove({dim!r}, ...)`"
    self._refuse_one_of(dim, call)
    if dim in self.schema.multi_dims:
        if not is_frame(labels) and not labels:
            return
        rel = self._tuples(dim, self._tuple_frame(dim, labels, {}, call), call)
        table = self._ensure(f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{dim}")
        self._delete(table, rel, dim, col("t", dim))
        return
    labels = _plain_labels(dim, labels, call)
    if not labels:
        return
    self._require_typed(dim, labels, call)
    self._require_unnamed(dim, labels)
    gone = self._columns_relation(
        {dim: list(labels)}, {dim: self._column_type(dim)}
    )
    staged = self.dims
    for m in self.schema.multi_dims:
        fields = [f for f, d in self.schema.over(m).items() if d == dim]
        if not fields or m not in staged:
            continue
        naming = reduce(
            operator.or_,
            (_field_in(m, f, labels) for f in fields),
        )
        if not staged[m].filter(naming).limit(1).fetchall():
            continue
        table = self._ensure(f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{m}")
        for f in fields:
            self._delete(table, gone, dim, col("t", m)[f])
    table = self._ensure(f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{dim}")
    self._delete(table, gone, dim, col("t", dim))

@_atomic
def rollback(self) -> None:
    """Clear every staged row without writing.

    Notes
    -----
    - [WorkingRecord](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/)
    """
    for kind, attribute in self._touched:
        self.con.execute(f"DELETE FROM {self._staged[kind, attribute]}")
        self._fill(kind, attribute)
        if kind == _ATTRIBUTES:
            self.con.execute(f"DELETE FROM {self._staged[_OWNERS, attribute]}")
    self._touched.clear()

docs.text:
Record(
    revision_id: UUID,
    sources: list[LayerSource],
    workspace: Workspace,
)

A record's layers folded last-writer-wins, read as DuckDB relations.

One class for every backing, because a fold over one source degenerates to a scan of it - so a plain parquet directory is read as the one layer it is (Workspace.at) rather than by a second code path. RecordLike is the protocol a caller annotates against; this is the class a caller holds.

Nothing up to the last frozen source can go stale, so the fold over them is kept in shared tables. A source after it is folded onto those tables per read, so a staged edit reads back with nothing to invalidate. The record holds those tables from construction until close(); one collected unclosed leaves them to the workspace.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default revision_id UUID

The node whose frozen layers are folded, which names the shared tables their fold is kept in.

required sources list of LayerSource

Root first, ending in the layer being resolved, truncated at the deepest materialised ancestor (sources_to_read). A WorkingRecord's staged rows are one more source on the end.

required workspace Workspace

Where the calling thread's cursor comes from.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

On a read once the record is closed.

Notes

  • a layer's data is write-once
  • materialised node caches
  • the owner map

Source code in src/datarecord/resolve/record.py 
def register(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Create the DuckDB schema `name` with a view per dim, property subject and attribute.

    The views sit in `name.dims`, `name.properties` and `name.attributes`,
    each reading as its relation here; over a `WorkingRecord` they follow
    every edit. They hold the tables the record reads, its folds and a
    `WorkingRecord`'s staging tables, until `unregister(name)`, whether
    the record is closed or not. `name` is listed in the workspace's
    `registered()` table.

    Raises
    ------
    duckdb.CatalogException
        If the schema `name` exists, as `_fold`, `_staged` and `_scratch`
        always do.
    ValueError
        If `name` is a database attached to the workspace, which DuckDB
        would read as the catalog of the nested schemas.
    duckdb.TransactionException
        Where the cursor already holds an open transaction.

    Notes
    -----
    - [registered views](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#registered-views)
    """
    con = self.con
    if (name,) in con.sql(
        "SELECT database_name FROM duckdb_databases()"
    ).fetchall():
        msg = f"`{name}` names a database attached to the workspace; register under another name"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    kinds = {
        "dims": self.dims,
        "properties": self.properties,
        "attributes": self.attributes,
    }
    rendered = {
        (name, kind, view): _render(rel, literals=True, wrap_text=True)[0]
        for kind, relations in kinds.items()
        for view, rel in relations.items()
    }
    holds = self.workspace._holds
    with transaction(
        con,
        "register",
        "https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#registered-views",
    ) as on_rollback:
        con.execute(f"CREATE SCHEMA {col(name)}")
        holds.hold(name, self._kept_schemas)
        on_rollback(partial(holds.release, name))
        for kind in kinds:
            con.execute(f"CREATE SCHEMA {col(name, kind)}")
        for path, query in rendered.items():
            con._create_view(path, query)
        con.execute(
            "INSERT INTO registered (name, revision, working, held)"
            " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            [
                name,
                self.revision_id,
                not self.frozen,
                sorted(self._kept_schemas),
            ],
        )

def select(record: RecordLike, /, **labels: Any) -> Selection:
    """`record` at the labels named, as xarray's `sel` takes them.

    A keyword names a dim; one naming a multi-dim's coordinate that is no dim
    narrows its tuples, and any other names a property by its bare name and
    narrows its subject to the labels whose value, its default applied, is
    selected. One label squeezes its dim. A list, a slice (both ends
    inclusive, `None` open) or a partial date string on a datetime axis keeps
    it. Every label referring to a dropped one goes with it, through
    properties and multi-dim tuples, until nothing more goes. Over a
    `Selection`, its keywords are merged and its base selected.

    Returns
    -------
    Selection
        The view, which reads the axes it matched and propagated on as they
        were at the call, and plans every attribute on the base's connection.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming the keyword: one naming no dim, coordinate or property, a
        multi-dim, a coordinate of several multi-dims or a property several
        subjects declare; a label the axis lacks; an empty list; a slice with
        a step, of an axis neither numeric nor datetime, with an end the axis
        cannot compare or covering no label; a squeezed label another
        keyword's selection drops; a squeeze folding a category into the
        default a kept label NULL on it does not take; squeezing every dim of
        a record with attributes.

    Notes
    -----
    - [selecting](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/selecting/)
    - [what goes with a dropped label](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/selecting/#what-goes-with-a-dropped-label)
    """
    if isinstance(record, Selection):
        return record.select(**labels)
    schema = record.schema
    read = _Read(record)
    asked: dict[str, Any] = {}
    squeezed: dict[str, Any] = {}
    kept: dict[str, set[Any]] = {}
    for keyword, value in labels.items():
        if keyword in schema.multi_dims:
            raise _refusal(
                keyword,
                value,
                "names a multi-dim, whose tuples are selected through its coordinates",
            )
        if keyword in schema.dimensions:
            matched = _match(
                keyword, value, read.axis(keyword), _dtype(schema, keyword)
            )
            asked[keyword] = matched
            if not isinstance(matched, list):
                squeezed[keyword] = matched
            _narrow(kept, keyword, {_key(m) for m in _listed(matched)})
            continue
        subject, allowed, asked[keyword] = _narrowing(schema, read, keyword, value)
        _narrow(kept, subject, allowed)
    for m in schema.multi_dims:
        over = schema.over(m)
        if all(d in squeezed for d in over.values()):
            squeezed[m] = {c: squeezed[d] for c, d in over.items()}
            _narrow(kept, m, {_key(t) for t in read.axis(m)})
    if schema.attributes and schema.dimensions.keys() <= squeezed.keys():
        raise _refused(
            {k: v for k, v in asked.items() if k in squeezed},
            "squeezes every dim, and attributes over no axis are no record; "
            "keep one dim as a list of one",
        )
    _propagate(schema, read, kept)
    for keyword, label in asked.items():
        if keyword in squeezed and _key(label) not in kept[keyword]:
            raise _refusal(
                keyword,
                label,
                "is squeezed at a label the selection drops through another keyword",
            )
    _refuse_uncategorized(schema, read, squeezed, kept)
    narrowed = {
        d: numbered_relation(
            record.con,
            d,
            [label for label in read.axis(d) if _key(label) in keys],
            _dtype(schema, d),
            _AT,
        )
        for d, keys in kept.items()
        if d in squeezed or len(keys) < len(read.axis(d))
    }
    view = _schema(schema, squeezed, read.category(squeezed))
    return Selection(record, asked, view, squeezed, narrowed)

def lift(self, attribute: str, rel: DuckDBPyRelation) -> DuckDBPyRelation:
    """`rel`, rows of `attribute` over this view, with the squeezed labels put back.

    Each squeezed dim the base declares `attribute` over is added as a
    column at its label, and each squeezed coordinate back into its
    multi-dim's struct; a NULL struct stays NULL. An attribute the base
    declares over no squeezed dim comes back as it came.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the base declares no `attribute`.

    Notes
    -----
    - [lifting rows back](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/selecting/#lift)
    """
    base = self.base.schema
    coordinates = base.coordinates_of(attribute)
    changed = [
        c
        for c in coordinates
        if c in self._squeezed or (c in rel.columns and self._shrunk(c))
    ]
    if not changed:
        return rel
    lifted: list[Expression] = []
    for c in coordinates:
        if c in self._squeezed:
            lifted.append(_literal(self._squeezed[c], self._type(c)).alias(c))
        elif c in changed:
            fields = {
                f: col(c)[f]
                if f in self.schema.over(c)
                else _literal(self._squeezed[d], self._type(d))
                for f, d in base.over(c).items()
            }
            lifted.append(_tuple(c, fields, self._type(c)))
        elif c in rel.columns:
            lifted.append(col(c))
    rest = [col(c) for c in rel.columns if c not in coordinates]
    return rel.project(*lifted, *rest)
