def settle(
    rel: DuckDBPyRelation,
    labels: Mapping[str, DuckDBPyRelation],
    flags: Flags,
    *,
    filter: bool = True,
) -> DuckDBPyRelation:
    """Settle the long rows of `rel` by the broadcast rule, one row per coordinate.

    A row NULL on a coordinate in `labels` takes each label there, and a row
    naming a label outside `labels`, or reaching none, is dropped. At each
    coordinate the row naming every coordinate in `labels` that the other rows
    there name is kept. A coordinate outside `labels` is kept as written, a
    NULL there being one more label, and `breakpoint` is no coordinate, so a
    curve is kept or dropped whole.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels
        Per coordinate, a relation holding its labels, or its tuples for a
        multi-dim, in a column of the coordinate's name.
    flags
        The attribute's `Flags`, or flags overstating them; they only spare
        work, so overstating changes no value.
    filter
        False keeps a row naming a label outside `labels` as written, for a
        caller whose own joins on the labels drop it anyway.

    Raises
    ------
    duckdb.Error
        On fetch, where no row names every coordinate the rows reaching it name.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the broadcast rule](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#the-broadcast-rule)
    - [settling rows](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/record/#settle)
    """
    over = [d for d in labels if d in rel.columns and (filter or d in flags.broadcast)]
    mixed = [d for d in over if d in flags.broadcast and d in flags.varies]
    if mixed:
        rel = rel.project(star(), named_mask(mixed).alias("_named"))
    for d in over:
        rows = rel.set_alias("_r")
        if d not in flags.broadcast:
            axis = labels[d].project(col(d)).set_alias("_ax")
            rel = rows.join(axis, col("_r", d) == col("_ax", d), how="semi")
        elif filter:
            rel = _broadcast_onto(rows, labels[d], d)
        else:
            rel = _broadcast_beside(rows, labels[d], d)
    if not mixed:
        return rel
    coordinates = [c for c in rel.columns if c not in ("_named", "breakpoint", "value")]
    coordinate = fn.concat_ws(
        lit(", "),
        *(
            fn.concat(
                lit(f"{c}="), coalesce(col(c).cast(sqltypes.VARCHAR), lit("NULL"))
            )
            for c in coordinates
        ),
    )
    crossed = fn.error(
        fn.concat(
            lit("two rows cross at "),
            coordinate,
            lit(
                " and no row reaching it names both, so neither is the more specific "
                "there (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#the-broadcast-rule)"
            ),
        )
    )
    return most_specific(rel, coordinates, crossed)

def coordinates_of(self, attribute: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The coordinate columns one attribute's rows carry, multi-dims first.

    A multi-dim in `dims` is carried as one struct column named for it, so
    `dims={"connection", "snapshot"}` gives `("connection", "snapshot")`.

    Per attribute rather than schema-wide: one file per attribute means one
    column set per attribute, and an all-NULL column of a dim the attribute
    is not addressed by would claim a coordinate the value has none of.

    Raises

    KeyError

def duck_type(self, spec: Dimension | AttributeSpec | PropertySpec) -> DuckDBPyType:
    """Return the DuckDB type of a declared dim, attribute or property.

    A dim with `one_of` has the `ENUM` of them, a multi-dim the struct of
    a field per coordinate, typed as the dim it draws on. A property that
    refers to a dim has the type of that dim.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#dtypes)
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#multi-dims)
    """
    if isinstance(spec, PropertySpec) and spec.one_of is not None:
        return self.duck_type(self.dimensions[spec.one_of])
    if isinstance(spec, Dimension) and spec.over is not None:
        return duckdb.struct_type(
            {c: self.duck_type(self.dimensions[d]) for c, d in spec.over.items()}
        )
    if isinstance(spec, Dimension) and spec.one_of is not None:
        return enum_type(spec.one_of)
    return DUCK_TYPES[cast("str", spec.dtype)]

def check_multi_dim_columns(
    self,
    multi_dims: Iterable[str],
    rel: DuckDBPyRelation,
    *,
    carrier: str,
) -> None:
    """Reject each of `multi_dims` carried other than as one struct column of exactly its coordinates.

    Judged by the relation's columns and types, so no row is read. A
    carrier without a multi-dim's column passes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    carrier
        What carries the columns, named in the message.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On a coordinate as a column of its own, or a multi-dim column not
        a struct of exactly the coordinates, naming the struct to pass
        instead.

    Notes
    -----
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#multi-dims)
    """
    types = dict(zip(rel.columns, rel.types, strict=True))
    for multi in multi_dims:
        key = list(self.over(multi))
        flat = [c for c in key if c in types]
        dtype = types.get(multi)
        fields = (
            key
            if dtype is None
            else [name for name, _ in dtype.children]
            if dtype.id == "struct"
            else None
        )
        if flat or fields is None or set(fields) != set(key):
            carried = f"{flat} flat" if flat else f"{multi!r} as {dtype}"
            msg = (
                f"{carrier} carries {carried}; pass {multi!r} as one struct "
                f"column with a field per coordinate, {key} (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#multi-dims)"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)

def refuse_partial_tuples(
    self,
    multi_dims: Iterable[str],
    rel: DuckDBPyRelation,
    *,
    carrier: str,
) -> None:
    """Reject a struct of any of `multi_dims` in `rel` with some fields NULL and not all.

    Reads the rows, unlike `check_multi_dim_columns`. A carrier without a
    multi-dim's column passes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    carrier
        What carries the columns, named in the message.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming `carrier` and the multi-dim.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the broadcast rule](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#the-broadcast-rule)
    """
    for multi in multi_dims:
        if multi not in rel.columns:
            continue
        some = reduce(
            operator.or_, (col(multi)[c].isnull() for c in self.over(multi))
        )
        partly = col(multi).isnotnull() & some
        if rel.filter(partly).limit(1).fetchall():
            msg = (
                f"{carrier} carries a {multi!r} with some fields NULL; a "
                f"multi-dim value is a whole tuple, or NULL for every tuple (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#the-broadcast-rule)"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)

def require_one_of(
    self, subject: str, data: Mapping[str, Iterable[Any]], what: str
) -> None:
    """Refuse a label its dim does not list.

    `data` maps column names to values. A name is checked where it is
    `subject` and `subject` has `one_of`, or where it is a property of
    `subject` that refers to a dim with `one_of`. Other names
    and NULL values are skipped.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming `what`, the column, the unknown labels and the dim's
        `one_of` labels.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#dtypes)
    """
    specs = self.properties.get(subject, {})
    for name, values in data.items():
        if name in specs:
            labels = self._one_of_labels(specs[name])
        elif name == subject and subject in self.dimensions:
            labels = self._one_of_labels(self.dimensions[subject])
        else:
            continue
        if labels is None:
            continue
        unknown = sorted({str(v) for v in values if v is not None} - {*labels})
        if unknown:
            msg = (
                f"{what} gives {name!r} labels {unknown}, which its dim's "
                f"`one_of` does not hold; `one_of` is {list(labels)}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)

def default_for(self, name: str, **categories: str) -> Any:
    """The default of attribute or `subject.name` property `name` for a label of `categories`.

    `categories` are keyed by each categorizing property's own name. The
    first `default_by` key listing the label's category decides, else
    `default`; a category left out matches none.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        As `resolve` does, and on a coordinate, which has no default.

    Notes
    -----
    - [AttributeSpec](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#attributes)
    - [default_by](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#default_by)
    """
    resolved = self.resolve(name)
    spec = resolved[1] if isinstance(resolved, tuple) else resolved
    if isinstance(spec, Dimension):
        msg = f"{name!r} is a coordinate, part of its multi-dim's key, and has no default"
        raise KeyError(msg)
    for key, by in spec.default_by.items():
        category = categories.get(key.partition(".")[2])
        if category in by:
            return by[category]
    return spec.default

def resolve(
    self, name: str
) -> AttributeSpec | tuple[str, PropertySpec] | tuple[str, Dimension]:
    """What `name` addresses: an attribute, or a property or coordinate as `subject.name`.

    Read off the name alone: a plain name is never a property.

    Returns
    -------
    AttributeSpec or tuple of str and PropertySpec or Dimension
        The attribute's spec, a property's subject and spec, or a
        coordinate's multi-dim and the dim the coordinate draws on.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If `name` addresses nothing; for a plain name some subject's
        property is called, naming each dotted form.

    Notes
    -----
    - [properties](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#properties)
    - [coordinates](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#multi-dims)
    """
    subject, dot, prop = name.partition(".")
    if dot:
        spec = self.properties.get(subject, {}).get(prop)
        if spec is not None:
            return subject, spec
        drawn = self.over(subject).get(prop) if subject in self.dimensions else None
        if drawn is None:
            msg = f"the schema declares no property {name!r}"
            raise KeyError(msg)
        return subject, self.dimensions[drawn]
    attribute = self.attributes.get(name)
    if attribute is not None:
        return attribute
    dotted = sorted(
        f"`{s}.{name}`" for s, specs in self.properties.items() if name in specs
    )
    hint = f"; did you mean {' or '.join(dotted)}" if dotted else ""
    msg = f"the schema declares no attribute {name!r}{hint}"
    raise KeyError(msg)

def owned_per(self, attribute: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Which dims a layer owns `attribute` per.

    Derived rather than declared: `AttributeSpec.dims` says which axes the
    attribute may vary over, `partial_dims` the fold key (the `partial`
    dims), and ownership is their intersection. A
    dim in `dims` but not the fold key - a non-`partial` value axis like
    `timestep` - is owned whole, so a patch to one of its values restates the
    attribute's entire extent along it (`_owned_whole`).

    Notes
    -----
    - [partial](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/layers/#partial)
    - [one fold for every axis](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/resolution/#axes)
    """
    spec = self.attributes.get(attribute)
    if spec is None:
        return frozenset()
    return spec.dims & set(self.partial_dims)

    self, column: str, subject: str | None = None

    - [the owner map](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/resolution/#the-owner-map)
    """
    found = self.declared(column, subject)
    return None if found is None else found[1]

def declared(
    self, column: str, subject: str | None = None, attribute: str | None = None
) -> tuple[str, DuckDBPyType, str] | None:
    """Look up the declaration of `column`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    subject
        The dim whose file holds the column. A column named like
        one of its properties is that property, named `subject.name`.
    attribute
        The attribute whose long rows hold the column. Its `value` column
        is the attribute, named as it is.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str, DuckDBPyType and str, or None
        The declared name, the DuckDB type, and the dtype as an error
        message shows it; None where the schema declares no type for
        `column`.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#dtypes)
    """
    own = self.properties.get(subject or "", {})
    spec: Dimension | AttributeSpec | PropertySpec
    if attribute is not None and column == "value":
        name, spec = attribute, self.attributes[attribute]
    elif column in own:
        name, spec = f"{subject}.{column}", own[column]
    elif column in self.dimensions and column not in STRUCTURAL_TYPES:
        name, spec = column, self.dimensions[column]
    else:
        duck = self._structural_type(column)
        return None if duck is None else (column, duck, str(duck))
    duck = self.duck_type(spec)
    return name, duck, f"{_typed_as(spec)} ({duck})"

def require_takes(
    self,
    rel: DuckDBPyRelation,
    what: str,
    subject: str | None = None,
    attribute: str | None = None,
) -> DuckDBPyRelation:
    """Check that each column of `rel` has a type that fits its declaration, and return `rel`, with its all-NULL columns cast to their declared types.

    A column type fits where `takes` says so. A column
    that fails this but holds only NULLs passes and is cast to its declared
    type, because dataframe libraries guess the type of an empty or
    all-None column. Only such columns have their rows read. `subject` and
    `attribute` are as in `declared`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming `what`, and for each refused column its type, its
        declared name and its dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#dtypes)
    - [set](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#set)
    """
    wrong = []
    nulls: dict[str, DuckDBPyType] = {}
    for c, given in zip(rel.columns, rel.types, strict=True):
        found = self.declared(c, subject, attribute)
        if found is None or takes(found[1], given):
            continue
        if not rel.filter(col(c).isnotnull()).limit(1).fetchall():
            nulls[c] = found[1]
            continue
        name, _, shown = found
        wrong.append(
            f"column {c!r} has type {given}, which does not fit {name!r} "
            f"of dtype {shown}"
        )
    if wrong:
        msg = f"{what}: {'; '.join(wrong)}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if not nulls:
        return rel
    return rel.project(
        *(
            col(c).cast(nulls[c]).alias(c) if c in nulls else col(c)
            for c in rel.columns
        )
    )

def compatible_with(self, other: Schema) -> list[str]:
    """Why layers written under `other` would not read under `self`.

    Empty when the change is compatible: old layers stay readable and only
    `version` moves. The compatible changes are those where NULL already
    means what the new schema needs it to mean, so the broadcast rule absorbs
    them without touching a row.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        One reason per incompatibility, empty if there are none.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the broadcast rule](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#the-broadcast-rule)
    - [versioning](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#compatibility)
    """
    problems = []

    for dim, was in other.dimensions.items():
        now = self.dimensions.get(dim)
        if now is None:
            problems.append(f"dim {dim!r} removed")
            continue
        if _typed_as(now) != _typed_as(was):
            problems.append(f"dim {dim!r} {_typed_as(was)} -> {_typed_as(now)}")

    for attr, was_spec in other.attributes.items():
        now_spec = self.attributes.get(attr)
        if now_spec is None:
            problems.append(f"attribute {attr!r} removed")
            continue
        if now_spec.dtype != was_spec.dtype:
            problems.append(
                f"attribute {attr!r} dtype {was_spec.dtype} -> {now_spec.dtype}"
            )
        narrowed = was_spec.dims - now_spec.dims
        if narrowed:
            problems.append(
                f"attribute {attr!r} no longer varies over {sorted(narrowed)}; "
                f"rows setting those dims have no valid reading"
            )

    for dim, specs in other.properties.items():
        for name, was_prop in specs.items():
            now_prop = self.properties.get(dim, {}).get(name)
            if now_prop is None:
                problems.append(f"property {name!r} of {dim!r} removed")
            elif _typed_as(now_prop) != _typed_as(was_prop):
                problems.append(
                    f"property {name!r} of {dim!r} {_typed_as(was_prop)} "
                    f"-> {_typed_as(now_prop)}"
                )

    if other.partial is not None and self.partial is not None:
        lost = other.partial - self.partial
        if lost:
            problems.append(
                f"{sorted(lost)} no longer `partial`; a layer that patched one "
                f"value along such an axis is now a partial override of an axis "
                f"owned whole"
            )
    return problems

def __init__(self, database: str = ":memory:") -> None:
    self._db = duckdb.connect(database)
    self._db.execute(_SCHEMAS)
    self._db.execute(_REVISIONS)
    self._db.execute(_REGISTERED)
    for schema in (FOLD, STAGED, SCRATCH):
        self._db.execute(f"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {col(schema)}")
    self._cursors = _Cursors(self._db)
    self._holds = _Holds(self._db)
    for name, held in self._db.execute(
        "SELECT name, held FROM registered"
    ).fetchall():
        self._holds.hold(name, held)
    self._stores: dict[str, Store] = {}
    self._schemas: dict[str, Schema] = {}
    self._local = LocalFiles()
    self._remote: Files | None = None
    self._remote_lock = threading.Lock()

def unregister(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Drop the schema `name` a record registered, with its views and its `registered()` row.

    A closed `WorkingRecord`'s staging tables go with its last registration.

    Raises
    ------
    duckdb.CatalogException
        If `name` is not registered, so a schema no record registered is
        never dropped.
    duckdb.TransactionException
        Where the cursor already holds an open transaction.

    Notes
    -----
    - [registered views](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#registered-views)
    """
    con = self.con
    with transaction(
        con,
        "unregister",
        "https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#registered-views",
    ):
        deleted = con.execute(
            "DELETE FROM registered WHERE name = ? RETURNING name", [name]
        ).fetchall()
        if not deleted:
            msg = f"no record is registered as `{name}` (`Workspace.registered()`)"
            raise duckdb.CatalogException(msg)
        con.execute(f"DROP SCHEMA {col(name)} CASCADE")
    self._holds.release(name)

def files(self, uri: str) -> Files:
    """The `Files` for `uri`'s scheme: local without `://`, remote for `s3://`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For any other scheme.
    """
    if "://" not in uri:
        return self._local
    if not uri.startswith("s3://"):
        msg = f"{uri}: a location is a local path or an s3:// URI"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    with self._remote_lock:
        if self._remote is None:
            self._remote = self._connect_remote()
        return self._remote

def at(self, uri: str) -> Record:
    """The standalone record at `uri`, read under its own `manifest.json`.

    A local `uri` is resolved, as `store` resolves one, so a later `chdir`
    cannot point it at another record.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If `uri` has no manifest, as where its write failed.
    ValueError
        If the manifest names a parent: a layer of a tree is read alone
        through its store's `layer(id)`.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the record format](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/)
    """
    base = _absolute(uri) + "/"
    manifest = Manifest.read(
        self.files(base), base + "manifest.json", self._schemas
    )
    if manifest is None:
        msg = f"{base} has no manifest.json, so holds no record"
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)
    if manifest.parent is not None:
        msg = (
            f"{base} is a layer over revision {manifest.parent}; a layer of a "
            f"tree is read alone through its store's `layer(id)`"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return _one_layer(base, manifest, self, manifest.id)

def write(
    self, source: LayerData | RecordLike, uri: str, *, meta: Meta | None = None
) -> Record:
    """Write `source` as a standalone record at `uri`, and read it back.

    A standalone record is one layer at its own URI, written to a URI that
    does not exist yet: its data first, then its manifest, with a fresh id
    and no parent, so one whose write failed reads as no record and one
    written again elsewhere is never read as the one before it. A failed
    write leaves its data files at `uri`, locally as remotely, for the
    caller to delete before writing there again.

    Raises
    ------
    FileExistsError
        If anything exists at `uri`: locally the path, even an empty
        directory; remotely any key under it.

    Notes
    -----
    - [writing a whole record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/layers/)
    - [a standalone directory](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/store/#a-standalone-directory)
    """
    base = _absolute(uri) + "/"
    meta = validate_meta(meta)
    if self.files(base).exists(base):
        msg = (
            f"{base} already exists; a standalone record is written to a URI "
            f"that does not exist yet"
        )
        raise FileExistsError(msg)
    data = layer_data(source, self.con)
    schema = data.schema
    files = write_layer(data, base, self)
    manifest = Manifest(
        id=uuid4(), parent=None, schema=schema, files=files, meta=meta
    )
    manifest.write(self.files(base), base + "manifest.json")
    return self.at(base)

def claim(self, *, parent: Revision | None, meta: Meta | None = None) -> Claim:
    """Hand out a new layer id under `parent`, by its create-only `claim.json`.

    The layer is pending, reached by no read, until `Claim.commit` writes
    its manifest; `meta` is the revision's, which the commit may extend
    but not change.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `parent` is a revision of another store, naming both locations.
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If `meta` is not flat, each value a string, finite number or boolean.

    Notes
    -----
    - [a revision exists only by its file](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/store/#a-revision-exists-only-by-its-manifest)
    """
    if parent is not None and parent.store.uri != self.uri:
        msg = (
            f"revision {parent.id} is of the store at {parent.store.uri}, so "
            f"it is no parent in the store at {self.uri}"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    claimed = ClaimFile(
        id=uuid4(),
        parent=None if parent is None else parent.id,
        meta=validate_meta(meta),
        created=datetime.now(UTC),
    )
    claimed.write(self.files, self.claim_uri(claimed.id))
    return Claim(store=self, **asdict(claimed))

def commit(
    self,
    source: LayerData | RecordLike,
    *,
    parent: Revision | None | _Base = _Base.OF_WORKING_RECORD,
    meta: Meta | None = None,
) -> Revision:
    """Write `source` as a new revision under `parent`: a claim and its commit in one.

    A `WorkingRecord` brings its parent, the revision it was built over,
    and is written as its edits, a delta against that revision. Any other
    source names its `parent`, `None` for a new root, and is written
    whole.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If a `WorkingRecord` comes with a `parent`, or any other source
        without one.
    ValueError
        If `w`'s base is no revision of this store, such as a standalone
        directory; as `claim` and `Claim.commit` do.

    Notes
    -----
    - [writing a whole record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/layers/)
    - [edits](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/editing/#edits)
    """
    if isinstance(source, WorkingRecord):
        if parent is not _Base.OF_WORKING_RECORD:
            msg = (
                "a `WorkingRecord` is written over the revision it was built "
                "over, so it takes no `parent`"
            )
            raise TypeError(msg)
        parent = self._base_of(source)
    elif parent is _Base.OF_WORKING_RECORD:
        msg = "`commit` needs a `parent=`, `None` for a new root"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    return self.claim(parent=parent, meta=meta).commit(source)

def revisions(self, *, meta: Meta | None = None) -> list[Revision]:
    """Every revision in this store whose `meta` holds each pair of `meta`, unordered.

    A pending layer is none. One listing of `layers/`, reading only the
    manifests the workspace does not already hold; a value matches only
    one of its own type, so `1` matches neither `1.0` nor `True`.

    Raises
    ------
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If `meta` is not flat, each value a string, finite number or boolean.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the layers](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/store/)
    """
    wanted = json.dumps(validate_meta(meta))
    self._scan()
    rows = self.workspace.con.execute(
        "SELECT id FROM revisions WHERE location = ? AND json_contains(meta, ?)",
        [self.uri, wanted],
    ).fetchall()
    return [Revision(id=id, store=self) for (id,) in rows]

def claims(self) -> list[Claim]:

def cleanup(
    self,
    *,
    ids: Iterable[UUID] | None = None,
    older_than: timedelta | None = None,
) -> list[UUID]:
    """Delete pending layers: those in `ids`, or those claimed `older_than` ago or earlier.

    Only a pending layer is deleted: each layer's manifest is rechecked
    right before its delete, without a lock. A job may hold its claim for
    days, so nothing deletes but this call, and a layer whose job still
    runs must be neither named nor young enough to match.

    Returns
    -------
    list of UUID
        The ids of the layers deleted.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        Unless exactly one of `ids` and `older_than` is given.
    ValueError
        Naming each of `ids` that is no pending layer, before anything is
        deleted.

    Notes
    -----
    - [cleanup](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/store/#cleanup)
    """
    match ids, older_than:
        case None, timedelta():
            cutoff = datetime.now(UTC) - older_than
            doomed = [c.id for c in self._claimed() if c.created <= cutoff]
        case Iterable(), None:
            doomed = list(dict.fromkeys(ids))
            pending = self._scan()
            refused = [str(i) for i in doomed if i not in pending]
            if refused:
                msg = (
                    f"{refused} are no pending layers of {self.uri}; cleanup "
                    f"deletes only a layer claimed and not committed"
                )
                raise ValueError(msg)
        case _:
            msg = "`cleanup` takes exactly one of `ids=` and `older_than=`"
            raise TypeError(msg)
    deleted = []
    for id in doomed:
        if self.files.exists(self.manifest_uri(id)):
            continue
        self.files.delete(self.layer_dir(id))
        deleted.append(id)
    return deleted

def commit(
    self, source: LayerData | RecordLike, *, meta: Meta | None = None
) -> Revision:
    """Write `source` as this claim's layer, then its manifest, which makes it a revision.

    The data goes straight into the layer directory; the manifest, written
    create-only and last, lists its files, its full schema, the claim's
    parent and the claim's `meta` with `meta` added. A `WorkingRecord` is
    written as its edits.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `meta` changes a key the claim set, `source` is edits staged
        over another revision than the claim's parent, the source's schema
        would make the parent's layers unreadable, the layer is committed
        already, or `source` fails validation. The layer is left pending.
    ValueError
        If `Store.cleanup` deleted the layer, before or while its data was
        written.
    PreconditionFailedError
        If another commit of this claim wrote the manifest first.
    KeyError
        If the claim's parent is gone from the store.
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If `meta` is not flat, each value a string, finite number or boolean.

    Notes
    -----
    - [a revision exists only by its file](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/store/#a-revision-exists-only-by-its-manifest)
    """
    store = self.store
    meta = merge_meta(self.meta, validate_meta(meta))
    if isinstance(source, WorkingRecord):
        source = source.edits
    if isinstance(source, StagedSource) and source.base != self.parent:
        msg = (
            f"these edits were staged over revision {source.base}, so they "
            f"are a delta against it and not against {self.parent}; commit "
            f"them as a child of the revision the `WorkingRecord` was built over"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if store.files.exists(store.manifest_uri(self.id)):
        msg = f"revision {self.id} is committed already; a claim commits once"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    self._refuse_cleaned_up()
    parent = None if self.parent is None else store.revision(self.parent)
    data = layer_data(source, store.workspace.con)
    schema = data.schema
    if parent is not None:
        problems = schema.compatible_with(parent.manifest.schema)
        if problems:
            msg = (
                f"this layer's schema is incompatible with its parent's: "
                f"{'; '.join(problems)} (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/schema/#compatibility)"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
    with nullcontext() if parent is None else parent.record as base:
        files = write_layer(
            data, store.layer_dir(self.id), store.workspace, parent=base
        )
    manifest = Manifest(
        id=self.id, parent=self.parent, schema=schema, files=files, meta=meta
    )
    self._refuse_cleaned_up()
    manifest.write(store.files, store.manifest_uri(self.id))
    store._cache([manifest])
    return Revision(id=self.id, store=store)

@classmethod
def read(
    cls, files: Files, uri: str, schemas: dict[str, Schema]
) -> Manifest | None:
    """The manifest at `uri`, or `None` where there is none.

    Its schema is taken from `schemas` by `schema_digest`, and parsed and
    added there only where it is missing.

    Raises
    ------
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If the manifest, or a schema not in `schemas`, is malformed.
    """
    found = files.read_text(uri)
    if found is None:
        return None
    raw = json.loads(found)
    text, digest = schema_digest(raw["schema"])
    if digest not in schemas:
        schemas[digest] = Schema.model_validate_json(text)
    return _MANIFEST.validate_python({**raw, "schema": schemas[digest]})

        parts.append(f"attributes {sorted(self.attributes)}")
    if self.unsupported_keys:
        unsupported = ", ".join(
            f"{dim} as {key}" for key, dim in sorted(self.unsupported_keys)
        )
        parts.append(f"unsupported keys ({unsupported})")
    if self.unsupported_dims:
        parts.append(f"unsupported dims {sorted(self.unsupported_dims)}")
    if self.unsupported_values:
        parts.append(f"unsupported values {sorted(self.unsupported_values)}")
    if self.names:
        parts.append(
            f"labels claimed by more than one category "
            f"{sorted(self.names)} (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#labels)"
        )
    return ", ".join(parts) if parts else "nothing"

def resolve(
    self,
    record: RecordLike,
    labels: Mapping[str, DuckDBPyRelation],
    flags: Mapping[str, Flags],
    *,
    filter: bool = True,
) -> DuckDBPyRelation:
    """This attribute's long relation, each source settled (`settle`) before `compute`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    flags
        Per source, its `Flags` as `settle` takes them.
    filter
        As `settle` takes it.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the Record protocol](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/record/)
    - [settling rows](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/record/#settle)
    """
    rels = [
        settle(record.attributes[s], labels, flags[s], filter=filter)
        for s in self.source
    ]
    if self.compute is None:
        return rels[0]
    return self.compute(*rels)

def requires(self, record: RecordLike) -> Requirements:
    """PyPSA's axes, the record's component types PyPSA knows, and their required attributes by source."""

build(record: RecordLike) -> Network

The resolved network.

A selection (Record.select) builds the network of its labels, selected once more as PyPSA holds it (_narrowed): a squeezed period is a single-period network without investment_period, a squeezed scenario a deterministic one, and kept scenarios' weights are renormalised. A record with a dim of its own is refused, as PyPSACollection builds it, and a selection at one label of that dim builds the member there.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If record is a selection squeezing a dim but period, scenario or a dim of its own, holding no snapshot, or keeping scenarios weighing nothing in all, or if an attribute's rows name several labels of a dim PyPSA holds it without (_unheld).

UnsupportedRecordError

If verify reports anything missing, a dim of the record's own included.

Notes
  • consuming a record
  • the broadcast rule
  • selecting before a build
Source code in src/datarecord/tools/pypsa.py 
def build(self, record: RecordLike) -> pypsa.Network:
    """The resolved network.

    A selection (`Record.select`) builds the network of its labels,
    selected once more as PyPSA holds it (`_narrowed`): a squeezed
    `period` is a single-period network without `investment_period`, a
    squeezed `scenario` a deterministic one, and kept scenarios' weights
    are renormalised. A record with a dim of its own is refused, as
    `PyPSACollection` builds it, and a selection at one label of that dim
    builds the member there.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `record` is a selection squeezing a dim but `period`,
        `scenario` or a dim of its own, holding no snapshot, or keeping
        scenarios weighing nothing in all, or if an attribute's rows name
        several labels of a dim PyPSA holds it without (`_unheld`).
    UnsupportedRecordError
        If `verify` reports anything missing, a dim of the record's own included.

    Notes
    -----
    - [consuming a record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/tools/)
    - [the broadcast rule](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/data-model/#the-broadcast-rule)
    - [selecting before a build](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/tools/#selecting-before-a-build)
    """
    record = _narrowed(record)
    flagged = record.flags()
    if unheld := _unheld(record, flagged):
        over = ", ".join(f"`{attr}` over {dims}" for attr, dims in unheld.items())
        msg = (
            f"A network holds one value of {over}, where the record holds "
            "several labels its rows name: select one label as a list of "
            "one, or build a network per `period` with `PyPSACollection`"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    missing, read = self._verify(record)
    if missing:
        raise UnsupportedRecordError(self.name, missing)

    con = record.con
    schema = record.schema
    shape = NetworkShape(schema, record.dims)
    n = _new_network(record, shape)

    periodless = {_INVESTMENT_PERIOD} if PERIOD in _squeezed(record) else set()
    over_entity = [
        a
        for a in schema.attributes
        if schema.addresses(a, ENTITY) and a not in periodless
    ]
    settled = _one_labelled(record)
    if shape.stochastic:
        settled[SCENARIO] = record.dims[SCENARIO]
    tuples = record.dims.get(CONNECTION)
    for ctype in _AXIS_TYPES:
        self._add_labels(n, record, ctype, flagged, shape, settled, con)
    _attach_sub_networks(n)
    for ctype, members in read.items():
        static = members.members
        if static is None:
            continue
        labels = {**settled, ENTITY: static}
        if tuples is not None:
            labels[CONNECTION] = _tuples_of(tuples, static)
        if not shape.stochastic and SCENARIO in static.columns:
            static = static.project(star(exclude=[SCENARIO]))
        static = static.project(star(), _POS)
        connections = members.connections
        static = _collapse_connections(static, connections, ctype, con)
        attributes = {}
        carried = _taken(schema, ctype, over_entity)
        for attr, flags in flagged.items():
            if attr not in carried:
                continue
            long = unpacked(
                schema,
                CONNECTION,
                self.schema.resolve(
                    record, ctype, attr, labels, flagged, filter=False
                ),
            )
            if CONNECTION in schema.attributes[attr].dims:
                for column, rows in _port_columns(
                    long, attr, connections, ctype, con
                ).items():
                    attributes[column] = (rows, flags)
            else:
                attributes[_INTERNAL_COLUMNS.get(attr, attr)] = (long, flags)

        _add_component_type(n, ctype, static, attributes, shape, con)

    _add_shapes(n, record)
    _broadcast_standard_types(n)
    return n

to_datarecord(
    model: Network,
    con: DuckDBPyConnection,
    *,
    results_only: bool = False,
    base: RecordLike | None = None,

Present a Network as the Record write_layer persists.

The inverse of build: static and series values become long rows on con, port columns connection rows carrying a role, buses and carriers the bus and carrier axes in PyPSA's order, "" NULL, and each shape the shape_{type} property of the label it outlines. Outputs are attributes like any other. A static value is left out where it repeats what the record resolves to without it: over base, base's value, else the default; over nothing, the default.

With results_only the record is a thin layer over base: the outputs, at their default too, base's output rows at the scenarios, buses, entities and connections the network holds that it does not write again restated as NULL, and this solve's SubNetworks as the sub_network axis, unless it holds fewer buses or entities than base, whose SubNetworks it then leaves. A series is written at the network's snapshots, base's standing at the others; over a multi-period base, a value over no snapshot is written for the entities active in the network's periods alone. base may be the selection the network was built from (Record.select): the layer is then over its record, each row at the labels it squeezes, one period squeezed writing at that period. Over the selection at one label of the record's dim of its own, the network is that member, written as PyPSACollection writes a collection of it alone.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If base is missing with results_only. If a network over a multi-period base whose investment periods it does not carry is written without results_only, or as results carries none and base squeezes none. If a full export is written over a selection or over a record with a dim of its own, or results over a record keeping one. If a deterministic network's results are written over a base holding scenarios, results over no scenario of fewer scenarios than the record holds, or a network's results holding a snapshot, bus or entity base lacks. On a full export: if types of one dim carry a custom property with different dtypes, a custom column is named shape_... or like snapshot, timestep, period, scenario, entity or connection, or a Shape carries one; if a shape lacks component, idx or type, two share all three, one on a PyPSA type names no member the network writes, or one's component names a dim PyPSA's schema declares; or if a custom text column named like a dim holds a value naming no label of it.

UnsupportedRecordError

If two entity types share a name.

Notes
  • ports
  • a label is unique within its dim
  • writing a whole record
  • writing results
  • a collection
Source code in src/datarecord/tools/pypsa.py 
def to_datarecord(
    self,
    model: pypsa.Network,
    con: DuckDBPyConnection,
    *,
    results_only: bool = False,
    base: RecordLike | None = None,
) -> RecordLike:
    """Present a `Network` as the `Record` `write_layer` persists.

    The inverse of `build`: static and series values become long rows on
    `con`, port columns connection rows carrying a `role`, buses and
    carriers the `bus` and `carrier` axes in PyPSA's order, `""` NULL,
    and each shape the `shape_{type}` property of the label it outlines.
    Outputs are attributes like any other. A static value is left out
    where it repeats what the record resolves to without it: over `base`,
    `base`'s value, else the default; over nothing, the default.

    With `results_only` the record is a thin layer over `base`: the
    outputs, at their default too, `base`'s output rows at the scenarios,
    buses, entities and connections the network holds that it does not
    write again restated as NULL, and this solve's SubNetworks as the
    `sub_network` axis, unless it holds fewer buses or entities than
    `base`, whose SubNetworks it then leaves. A series is written at the
    network's snapshots, `base`'s standing at the others; over a
    multi-period `base`, a value over no snapshot is written for the
    entities active in the network's periods alone. `base` may be the
    selection the network was built from (`Record.select`): the layer is
    then over its record, each row at the labels it squeezes, one period
    squeezed writing at that period. Over the selection at one label of
    the record's dim of its own, the network is that member, written as
    `PyPSACollection` writes a collection of it alone.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `base` is missing with `results_only`. If a network over a
        multi-period `base` whose investment periods it does not carry is
        written without `results_only`, or as results carries none and
        `base` squeezes none. If a full export is written over a
        selection or over a record with a dim of its own, or results over
        a record keeping one. If a deterministic network's results are
        written over a `base` holding scenarios, results over no
        `scenario` of fewer scenarios than the record holds, or a
        network's results holding a snapshot, bus or entity `base` lacks.
        On a full export: if types of one dim carry a custom property
        with different dtypes, a custom column is named `shape_...` or
        like `snapshot`, `timestep`, `period`, `scenario`, `entity` or
        `connection`, or a Shape carries one; if a shape lacks
        `component`, `idx` or `type`, two share all three, one on a PyPSA
        type names no member the network writes, or one's `component`
        names a dim PyPSA's schema declares; or if a custom text column
        named like a dim holds a value naming no label of it.
    UnsupportedRecordError
        If two entity types share a name.

    Notes
    -----
    - [ports](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/tools/#ports)
    - [a label is unique within its dim](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/format/#labels)
    - [writing a whole record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/layers/)
    - [writing results](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/tools/#writing-results)
    - [a collection](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/reference/tools/#a-collection)
    """
    _require_base(results_only, base)
    if not results_only and isinstance(base, Selection):
        msg = (
            "A full export is written over a record, not over a selection "
            "of one: its rows would miss the labels the selection squeezes"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    own = [] if base is None else _own_dims(_root(base).schema)
    squeezed: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if isinstance(base, Selection):
        squeezed = {d: base.labels[d] for d in _squeezed(base)}
    if own and (not results_only or len(own) > 1 or own[0] not in squeezed):
        msg = (
            f"A network is not written over a record with a dim of its own, "
            f"{own}, where its rows would reach every label: write its "
            f"results over the selection it was built from, "
            f"`record.select({own[0]}=label)`, or the collection with "
            "`PyPSACollection`"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if not results_only and base is not None and _multiperiod(base):
        periods = _axis_labels(base, PERIOD)
        if list(model.investment_periods) != periods:
            msg = (
                f"A network of investment periods {list(model.investment_periods)} "
                f"is written over a `base` of {periods} with "
                "`results_only=True` only"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
    source = self._source(model, con, base, results_only)
    if not own:
        return source
    (dim,) = own
    return _StackedSource.of({squeezed[dim]: source}, dim, con, base)

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Each tutorial takes you from nothing to a working result, one step at a time. Take them in order.

  • Your first record builds a record from a schema, commits it to a store and reads it back.
  • A scenario on a branch branches that record, overrides one value and materialises the child.
  • Solve a record with PyPSA solves a record with the PyPSA tool and commits the results.

docs.title: Your first record
docs.text:
In this tutorial you build a record of two generators, commit it to a store and read it back. It takes about 25 minutes.

You need datarecord installed, as Installation shows.

docs.title: The schema
docs.text:
A record's schema declares what the record may contain. It lists the sets of labels that values vary along (dims), the values that describe one label (properties) and the values over dims (attributes). The data model defines each. Run this:

from datarecord import AttributeSpec, Dimension, PropertySpec, Schema

schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": Dimension(dtype="str"),
        "ctype": Dimension(one_of=["Generator", "Load"]),
        "bus": Dimension(dtype="str"),
        "carrier": Dimension(dtype="str"),
        "snapshot": Dimension(dtype="int"),
        "connection": Dimension(over=["entity", "bus"]),
    },
    properties={
        "entity": {
            "ctype": PropertySpec(one_of="ctype"),
            "carrier": PropertySpec(one_of="carrier"),
        },
    },
    attributes={
        "p_nom": AttributeSpec(dtype="float", dims={"entity"}, default=0.0, unit="MW"),
        "p_max_pu": AttributeSpec(
            dtype="float", dims={"entity", "snapshot"}, default=1.0
        ),
    },
    partial={"entity", "bus", "connection"},
)
print(schema.dims)
print(schema.multi_dims)

Check it:

('entity', 'ctype', 'bus', 'carrier', 'snapshot')
('connection',)

connection is a dim whose labels are (entity, bus) tuples (a multi-dim), so the schema lists it apart from the five plain dims. ctype lists its labels in the schema with one_of, and partial lists the dims along which a later layer overrides one label's value.

docs.title: An empty root
docs.text:
A record is kept in one location (a store) as a tree of the data each commit adds (layers). You open each layer by its id (a revision). You stage edits over a revision, so the first revision has the schema and no rows. Any object with the members of RecordLike can be committed, and this dataclass has the fewest:

import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from duckdb import DuckDBPyConnection

from datarecord import Workspace


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Empty:
    schema: Schema
    con: DuckDBPyConnection
    dims: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    properties: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    attributes: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def flags(self, **categories):
        return {}


ws = Workspace()
store = ws.store(tempfile.mkdtemp())
root = store.commit(Empty(schema, ws.con), parent=None)
print(root.record.dims["entity"].df())

Check it:

Empty DataFrame
Columns: [entity]
Index: []

The root revision's entity dim has no labels. The Workspace is the DuckDB database that its stores share.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
A WorkingRecord stages edits over a revision. Add the labels:

from datarecord import WorkingRecord

w = WorkingRecord(root.record)
w.add("carrier", ["wind", "gas"])
w.add("bus", ["north", "south"])
w.add("entity", ["wind1", "gas1"], ctype="Generator", carrier=["wind", "gas"])
w.add(
    "connection",
    [{"entity": "wind1", "bus": "north"}, {"entity": "gas1", "bus": "south"}],
)
w.add("snapshot", [0, 1, 2])
print(w.properties["entity"].df())
print(w.dims["connection"].df())

Check it:

  entity      ctype carrier
0  wind1  Generator    wind
1   gas1  Generator     gas
                            connection
0  {'entity': 'wind1', 'bus': 'north'}
1   {'entity': 'gas1', 'bus': 'south'}

Each generator has its ctype and carrier properties, and each connection is one struct with an entity and a bus field. The carriers and buses come first, because add refuses a property value or a tuple field that is not yet a label of its dim.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
set stages attribute values at the labels you name:

w.set("p_nom", [100.0, 50.0], entity=["wind1", "gas1"])
w.set("p_max_pu", [0.3, 0.8, 0.5], entity="wind1", snapshot=[0, 1, 2])
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9, entity="gas1")
print(w.attributes["p_max_pu"].df())

Check it:

  entity  snapshot attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1         0  p_max_pu         NaN    0.3
1   gas1      <NA>  p_max_pu         NaN    0.9
2  wind1         1  p_max_pu         NaN    0.8
3  wind1         2  p_max_pu         NaN    0.5

attributes returns long rows, one per value, in no promised order. The gas1 row leaves snapshot NULL, and a NULL coordinate means every label of its dim (the broadcast rule).

docs.title: The values, wide
docs.text:
settle applies that rule and gives one row per label at each point, which pandas pivots wide:

from datarecord import settle

labels = {"entity": w.dims["entity"], "snapshot": w.dims["snapshot"]}
settled = settle(w.attributes["p_max_pu"], labels, w.flags()["p_max_pu"])
print(settled.df().pivot(index="snapshot", columns="entity", values="value"))

Check it:

entity    gas1  wind1
snapshot
0          0.9    0.3
1          0.9    0.8
2          0.9    0.5

settle turned the one gas1 row into a value of 0.9 at each of the three snapshots. properties is already wide, with one row per label.

docs.title: A committed revision
docs.text:
store.commit writes the staged edits as a layer, a child of the revision w was made over:

rev = store.commit(w)
print(rev.parent == root.id)

True

The new revision rev is a child of the root. Open it by its id and read it:

record = store.revision(rev.id).record
print(record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  100.0
1   gas1     p_nom         NaN   50.0

The committed revision contains the values you set. The root still has no rows, because a layer is written once and a commit never changes the parent:

w.close()
print(root.record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

Empty DataFrame
Columns: [entity, attribute, breakpoint, value]
Index: []

docs.title: What you have built
docs.text: You have built a store with two revisions. The root is empty, and its child contains two generators, their buses and connections, and values for p_nom and p_max_pu. You read the values long, as they are stored, and wide, with the broadcast rule applied.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
• A scenario on a branch branches this record and overrides one value.
  • Solve a record with PyPSA hands a record to PyPSA.
  • Read a record lists the other ways to read one.

docs.title: Solve a record with PyPSA
docs.text:
In this tutorial you build a record of a bus, two generators and a load, solve it with PyPSA and commit the results. It takes about 20 minutes, and it follows Your first record.

You need the PyPSA tool, which comes with PyPSA and the HiGHS solver:

pip install datarecord[pypsa]

PyPSA prints its own warnings and solver log as it runs, which the outputs below leave out.

docs.title: The tool's schema
docs.text:
The PyPSA tool is the module that translates between a record and PyPSA. It declares its schema from PyPSA's own registry. Export a network that has only its snapshots, and commit it as the root:

import tempfile

import pandas as pd
import pypsa

from datarecord import Workspace
from datarecord.tools.pypsa import PyPSA

ws = Workspace()
store = ws.store(tempfile.mkdtemp())

n = pypsa.Network(snapshots=pd.date_range("2030-01-01", periods=3, freq="h"))
root = store.commit(PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, ws.con), parent=None)
print(root.record.dims["snapshot"].df())
print(list(root.record.schema.properties["entity"]))

Check it:

             snapshot
0 2030-01-01 00:00:00
1 2030-01-01 01:00:00
2 2030-01-01 02:00:00
['ctype', 'carrier', 'sign', 'type']

The root has the three snapshots, and every entity takes the four properties that PyPSA keeps on a component.

docs.title: The components
docs.text:
A component is a label of entity, its type is its ctype, and each of its ports is a connection tuple with a role. Stage them over the root, with their values:

from datarecord import WorkingRecord

w = WorkingRecord(root.record)
w.add("carrier", ["AC", "wind", "gas"])
w.add("bus", ["north"])
w.add("entity", ["wind1", "gas1"], ctype="Generator", carrier=["wind", "gas"])
w.add("entity", ["load1"], ctype="Load")
w.add(
    "connection",
    [{"entity": e, "bus": "north"} for e in ["wind1", "gas1", "load1"]],
    role="attached",
)
w.set("p_nom", [100.0, 80.0], entity=["wind1", "gas1"])
w.set("marginal_cost", 50.0, entity="gas1")
w.set("p_max_pu", [0.9, 0.4, 0.1], entity="wind1", snapshot=list(n.snapshots))
w.set("p_set", 60.0, entity="load1")
print(PyPSA.verify(w).describe())

Check it:

nothing

verify reports what a record lacks for a PyPSA build, and here it lacks nothing. AC is there because a bus's carrier defaults to it.

docs.title: The network
docs.text:
Commit the inputs, then build a pypsa.Network from the revision:

inputs = store.commit(w)
net = PyPSA.build(inputs.record)
print(net.generators[["bus", "carrier", "p_nom", "marginal_cost"]])
print(net.generators_t.p_max_pu)

         bus carrier  p_nom  marginal_cost
name
wind1  north    wind  100.0            0.0
gas1   north     gas   80.0           50.0
name                 wind1
snapshot
2030-01-01 00:00:00    0.9
2030-01-01 01:00:00    0.4
2030-01-01 02:00:00    0.1

build turned each connection into its generator's bus, and wind1 takes the default marginal_cost.

docs.title: A solve
docs.text:
Solve the network with HiGHS:

print(net.optimize(solver_name="highs", log_to_console=False))
print(net.generators_t.p)

('ok', 'optimal')
name                 wind1  gas1
snapshot
2030-01-01 00:00:00   60.0  -0.0
2030-01-01 01:00:00   40.0  20.0
2030-01-01 02:00:00   10.0  50.0

Wind covers the load where it can, and gas covers the rest.

docs.title: A results revision
docs.text:
With results_only=True, to_datarecord presents only what the solve produced, as a layer over the record the network was built from. Commit it as a child of inputs:

results = PyPSA.to_datarecord(net, ws.con, results_only=True, base=inputs.record)
solved = store.commit(results, parent=inputs)
print(solved.parent == inputs.id)

True

solved is a child of inputs, and each result is an attribute like any other. Read the bus's price:

price = solved.record.attributes["marginal_price"].df()
print(price[["bus", "snapshot", "value"]])

     bus            snapshot  value
0  north 2030-01-01 00:00:00   -0.0
1  north 2030-01-01 01:00:00   50.0
2  north 2030-01-01 02:00:00   50.0

The price is gas's marginal cost wherever gas runs. A read of solved returns its parent's inputs too:

print(solved.record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

  scenario entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0     None  wind1     p_nom         NaN  100.0
1     None   gas1     p_nom         NaN   80.0

p_nom comes from inputs, with the scenario coordinate that the tool's schema declares left NULL.

docs.title: What you have built
docs.text: You have built a record that the PyPSA tool accepts and solved it. Its results are a child revision, and a read of it returns both the results and the inputs.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
• Use the PyPSA tool exports an existing network and checks it with verify.
  • Tools lists what the PyPSA tool reads from a record and writes back.
  • Present a framework object is for writing a tool of your own.

docs.title: A scenario on a branch
docs.text: In this tutorial you branch a high-wind scenario off a record, override one value in it and read the result through both revisions. It takes about 15 minutes, and it starts from the record of Your first record.

docs.title: The base record
docs.text:
Run this to build the record of the first tutorial again, committed as the revision base:

import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from duckdb import DuckDBPyConnection

from datarecord import (
    AttributeSpec,
    Dimension,
    PropertySpec,
    Schema,
    WorkingRecord,
    Workspace,
)

schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": Dimension(dtype="str"),
        "ctype": Dimension(one_of=["Generator", "Load"]),
        "bus": Dimension(dtype="str"),
        "carrier": Dimension(dtype="str"),
        "snapshot": Dimension(dtype="int"),
        "connection": Dimension(over=["entity", "bus"]),
    },
    properties={
        "entity": {
            "ctype": PropertySpec(one_of="ctype"),
            "carrier": PropertySpec(one_of="carrier"),
        },
    },
    attributes={
        "p_nom": AttributeSpec(dtype="float", dims={"entity"}, default=0.0, unit="MW"),
        "p_max_pu": AttributeSpec(
            dtype="float", dims={"entity", "snapshot"}, default=1.0
        ),
    },
    partial={"entity", "bus", "connection"},
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Empty:
    schema: Schema
    con: DuckDBPyConnection
    dims: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    properties: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    attributes: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def flags(self, **categories):
        return {}


ws = Workspace()
store = ws.store(tempfile.mkdtemp())
root = store.commit(Empty(schema, ws.con), parent=None)

with WorkingRecord(root.record) as w:
    w.add("carrier", ["wind", "gas"])
    w.add("bus", ["north", "south"])
    w.add("entity", ["wind1", "gas1"], ctype="Generator", carrier=["wind", "gas"])
    w.add(
        "connection",
        [{"entity": "wind1", "bus": "north"}, {"entity": "gas1", "bus": "south"}],
    )
    w.add("snapshot", [0, 1, 2])
    w.set("p_nom", [100.0, 50.0], entity=["wind1", "gas1"])
    w.set("p_max_pu", [0.3, 0.8, 0.5], entity="wind1", snapshot=[0, 1, 2])
    w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9, entity="gas1")
    base = store.commit(w)

print(base.record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

Check it:

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  100.0
1   gas1     p_nom         NaN   50.0

base has the values that the first tutorial set. The with block closed the WorkingRecord once its edits were committed.

docs.title: One edit
docs.text:
Stage the scenario's one change, a larger wind generator, over base:

w = WorkingRecord(base.record)
w.set("p_nom", 150.0, entity="wind1")
print(w.edits.attribute("p_nom").df())

Check it:

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  150.0

w.edits contains only what you staged: one row, and nothing of gas1.

docs.title: A child revision
docs.text:
Commit the edit with a meta entry for the scenario:

high = store.commit(w, meta={"scenario": "high"})
w.close()
print(high.parent == base.id, high.meta)

True {'scenario': 'high'}

high is a child of base. Committing a second WorkingRecord over base would give high a sibling on another branch.

docs.title: The fold
docs.text:
Read p_nom through high:

print(high.record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  150.0
1   gas1     p_nom         NaN   50.0

The step that combines a revision's layers (the fold) assigns each row to the deepest layer that wrote it. A read returns the child's wind1 row, and gas1 from base. Read p_nom through base:

print(base.record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  100.0
1   gas1     p_nom         NaN   50.0

base still has wind1 at 100. Read the child's layer alone:

print(store.layer(high.id).attributes["p_nom"].df())

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  150.0

The layer contains only the one row that the commit wrote.

docs.title: A materialised revision
docs.text:
A read of high folds every layer from the root down. Writing the fold's result beside the revision's layer (materialising it) lets a later read stop there:

import os

high.materialise()
print(sorted(os.listdir(store.resolved_dir(high.id))))

['dim_owners.parquet', 'owner_map.parquet']

The two files are the fold's result for high. Read the revision again:

record = store.revision(high.id).record
print(record.attributes["p_nom"].df())

  entity attribute  breakpoint  value
0  wind1     p_nom         NaN  150.0
1   gas1     p_nom         NaN   50.0

The values are the same. Materialising changes how many layers a read opens, and never what it returns.

docs.title: What you have built
docs.text: You have built a scenario as a child revision that contains one row, read it through the fold beside its unchanged parent, and materialised it.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:

  • Branch and materialise covers siblings, navigating the tree and claims.
  • Layers and the fold describe what a layer may contain and how rows of two layers combine.
